# Compliance Rules

## Portfolio scope: graph8, CIENCE, and Tenbound

Brand attribution: graph8 software plans, CIENCE managed-service fees, and Tenbound assessment fees are separate offers. Tenbound's published Programmable Revenue Blueprint is $1,000 for a three-week engagement. Confirm applicable scope and terms directly; do not imply guaranteed pipeline outcomes, independent endorsements, or a requirement to purchase graph8 or CIENCE after an assessment. Cite Tenbound when using its published frameworks.

---

# Compliance Rules

## Required Disclaimers

### All marketing pages, case studies, ROI calculators, and sales collateral referencing pipeline or revenue results
**Text:** Results vary. Pipeline outcomes depend on your ICP definition, market segment, campaign execution quality, and team adoption. graph8 does not guarantee specific meeting volumes, pipeline amounts, or revenue outcomes.
**When to use:** Whenever quantitative pipeline, revenue, meeting, or conversion outcomes are referenced in marketing materials

### Pricing page, plan comparison pages, data product pages, and onboarding documentation
**Text:** Fair-use rate limits apply on all plans. Limits are designed to prevent scraping and bulk resale, not to restrict legitimate GTM work. Excessive automated data export beyond normal sales operations may result in throttling or account review.
**When to use:** Whenever plan features, credit usage, or data access are described — especially on the graph8 pricing page

### CIENCE SDR Capacity pricing page, SDR services collateral, and any commission-related marketing or sales materials
**Text:** SDR commission rates and meeting fees are calculated based on agreed ROI goals and individual SDR performance targets. Commission is not paid below 60% of target. Between 60–99% of target, a reduced rate applies. At or above 100%, full rate applies. Individual SDR performance does not trigger bonuses for other SDRs on the same account.
**When to use:** Whenever SDR performance-based compensation, meeting fees, or commission structures are described or promoted

### Tenbound pricing page, Blueprint sales collateral, and proposal documents
**Text:** The Tenbound Programmable Revenue Blueprint is a fixed-scope, one-time assessment. No refunds are issued; clients retain all five deliverable documents regardless of downstream vendor decisions. Tenbound has no financial interest in which tools or vendors clients adopt after the engagement.
**When to use:** Whenever the Programmable Revenue Blueprint is offered, sold, or described in marketing materials

### Studio product pages, AI Agents product pages, AI Inbox product pages, and any collateral describing AI-generated outreach or content
**Text:** AI-generated content — including email copy, call scripts, battlecards, landing pages, and account intelligence — is produced by graph8 Studio and AI agents based on publicly available and user-provided data. Human review before sending or publishing is the responsibility of the customer. graph8 does not assume liability for AI-generated content sent to third parties without human review.
**When to use:** Whenever AI-generated content capabilities (Studio, SDR Agent, AI Inbox, AI Voice Agents) are described or demonstrated

### Dialer product page, AI Voice Agents product page, and all collateral describing voice cloning capabilities
**Text:** Voice cloning features require explicit consent from the individual whose voice is being cloned. Use of AI voice cloning for outbound calling without the rep's informed consent violates graph8's Terms of Service and may violate applicable law.
**When to use:** Any time voice cloning or rep voice replication features are mentioned in marketing, sales, or onboarding materials

### Signals product pages, visitor identification feature descriptions, and all collateral describing de-anonymization capabilities
**Text:** Visitor identification and de-anonymization capabilities resolve anonymous site traffic to company and individual-level records. Use of these features must comply with applicable privacy laws in the visitor's jurisdiction, including GDPR, CCPA, and other regional regulations. Customers are responsible for obtaining and maintaining appropriate consents and disclosures on their websites.
**When to use:** Whenever visitor identification, de-anonymization, or site-traffic resolution features are described

### Tenbound Standard page, Maturity Model page, all downloadable Tenbound framework documents, and any third-party republication of Tenbound research
**Text:** The Tenbound Pipeline Architecture Standard, Maturity Model, and associated frameworks are free to read, share, and build on. The one condition of use is attribution: cite Tenbound as the source and include a link to the original publication.
**When to use:** Whenever Tenbound's published frameworks (Pipeline Architecture Standard, Maturity Model, Ontology guidance) are referenced, reproduced, or cited

### Tenbound Blueprint sales collateral, engagement kick-off materials, and Tenbound website
**Text:** Session recording and transcription: Tenbound Programmable Revenue Blueprint engagements involve recording and transcription of all role-shadowing sessions. All participants are informed before sessions begin. Session recordings are used solely for analysis purposes and are not shared outside the engagement team.
**When to use:** Whenever the Blueprint engagement process is described, especially the week-one observation phase

### All sign-up pages, pricing pages, and free trial CTAs
**Text:** By signing up for graph8, you agree to graph8's Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Free plans include 1,000 contact reveals and 500 execution actions. No credit card is required to start. Credits are consumed when the system executes actions (sends, calls, agent runs); browsing and searching the buyer graph does not consume credits.
**When to use:** On every page or ad that includes a sign-up CTA, 'Start Free' button, or free trial offer

## Required Disclosures

### Privacy
- graph8 collects and processes personal data in accordance with its Privacy Policy (graph8.com/privacy). By using the platform, customers agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.
- Visitor identification features de-anonymize website traffic to company and individual level. Customers deploying these features on their own websites are responsible for disclosing this practice in their own privacy policies and obtaining necessary consents under GDPR, CCPA, and other applicable regulations.
- graph8 processes B2B contact data sourced from public and licensed third-party sources. Customers using this data for outreach are responsible for compliance with CAN-SPAM, CASL, GDPR, and other applicable anti-spam and data protection laws in target recipients' jurisdictions.
- Social listening features monitor public posts on X (Twitter) and other platforms for brand mentions and buying-intent signals. Only publicly available posts are monitored; no private communications are accessed.
- Tenbound Blueprint sessions are recorded and transcribed for analysis purposes only. All session participants are informed before recording begins. Recordings are not shared with third parties and are deleted after the engagement deliverables are finalized.
- graph8's AI agents (Chief of Staff, SDR Agent, RevOps Agent) operate within customer-defined guardrails. Customers control which actions agents may take autonomously (Read, Propose, or Act modes). All autonomous actions are logged and attributed.
- Voice cloning for AI Voice Agents requires the explicit, informed consent of the individual whose voice is cloned. Customers must obtain and document this consent before enabling voice cloning features.

### Pricing
- graph8 Team plan is $99/month for the full platform with unlimited users. The MCP Unlimited plan is $25/user/month. The Free/Pay-as-you-go tier starts at no cost with 1,000 contact reveals and 500 execution actions; additional credits cost $0.05 each.
- CIENCE GTM Setup Sprint is a one-time fee of $5,000. Performance-Driven Growth managed services are $2,000/month. The graph8 platform license for CIENCE-managed clients is $499/month (75,000 monthly credits included). First-month all-in cost is $7,499 before optional SDR capacity.
- CIENCE SDR Capacity is priced by level and geography: Level 1 (Scripted Outreach) $1,500–$4,500/month; Level 2 (Independent Producer) $2,500–$5,500/month; Level 3 (Data-Driven Optimizer) $3,500–$6,500/month. SDR onboarding and recruitment is $1,000 one-time per SDR.
- Tenbound Programmable Revenue Blueprint is $1,000 one-time. CIENCE Revenue System Standard Build is $9,500 for 60 days. Deployed Build is $25,000 for 60 days. The Tenbound Pipeline Architecture Standard and Maturity Model are free to read and use.
- Per-meeting fees for CIENCE-managed campaigns are calculated from the agreed ROI goal (typically 4x ROI) using the campaign calculator. These fees are not a flat published rate and must be confirmed in the client agreement.
- Scaled outbound credit tiers are available at discounts as volume grows. Contact CIENCE for volume pricing. Standard Team plan includes 10,000 execution credits/month; CIENCE-managed platform includes 75,000 credits/month.
- All graph8 plans are month-to-month with no annual contracts unless otherwise specified. Cancel anytime. 7-day free trial available on the Team plan with no credit card required.

### Data
- graph8's buyer graph contains 700M+ verified contacts and 100M+ companies. Emails and phone numbers are verified before delivery; records that fail verification are flagged and not delivered.
- Data accuracy is maintained through automated verification and waterfall enrichment across multiple third-party providers. Despite verification, data may become outdated; users are encouraged to re-enrich records regularly.
- Customers own all data they pull from the platform and may export it at any time. Exports consume contact data credits from the same credit pool as reveals and enrichments.
- Waterfall enrichment uses multiple third-party data providers. Customers may bring their own API keys and data vendor relationships; costs for third-party data consumed via the waterfall are charged on a pay-on-match basis.
- The buyer graph aggregates approximately 2 billion signals daily across visitor, intent, form, hiring, job change, social, tech stack, and funding sources. Signal accuracy and recency vary by source; intent scores are model-derived and should be used as prioritization signals, not as guaranteed purchase indicators.
- Tenbound Blueprint engagements require no system access. Observation is conducted via screen share only. Tenbound engineers review only publicly visible assets (website, forms, sending domain) plus any optional access granted by the client (e.g., Search Console, CRM).
- All AI agent actions within graph8 are logged, timestamped, and auditable. Customers can review every action an agent took, what data it read, and what it changed, via the Activity feed and audit trail.

## Industry Regulations

### CAN-SPAM Act
**Applies to:** All outbound email campaigns executed via graph8 Campaigns & Sequencer, CIENCE Scaled Outbound, CIENCE Managed SDR services, and AI Inbox auto-send features targeting US-based recipients

**Requirements:**
- Every commercial email must include a clear and conspicuous opt-out/unsubscribe mechanism
- Unsubscribe requests must be honored within 10 business days
- The sender's physical postal address must be included in every commercial email
- Subject lines must not be deceptive or misleading
- The email must be clearly identified as an advertisement if it is promotional in nature
- The 'From' name and email address must accurately identify the sending organization
- graph8 deliverability infrastructure must maintain suppression lists that are honored across all campaigns

**Impact on marketing:** All email sequences built in graph8 Sequencer and executed by CIENCE must include compliant footers with unsubscribe links and physical address. AI-drafted emails (via SDR Agent and AI Inbox) must include these elements before sending. Marketing materials promoting email outreach capabilities must note CAN-SPAM compliance as a built-in control.

### GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation)
**Applies to:** All data processing, outbound outreach, visitor identification, and signal monitoring involving contacts located in the European Economic Area; applicable to graph8 Platform (Data, Signals, Campaigns, AI Inbox, Dialer), CIENCE Europe SDR teams, and Tenbound Blueprint engagements with EU-based clients

**Requirements:**
- A lawful basis for processing personal data must be established and documented before data is used for outreach (e.g., legitimate interests assessment for B2B prospecting)
- Data subjects must be able to exercise rights of access, rectification, erasure, and portability
- Visitor identification and de-anonymization of EU-based website visitors requires disclosure in the site's privacy policy
- Data retention periods must be defined and enforced; stale or unused contact records should be purged per policy
- Any third-party data processors used in the waterfall enrichment pipeline must have signed Data Processing Agreements (DPAs)
- Cross-border data transfers (e.g., EU contact data processed on US servers) must be governed by Standard Contractual Clauses or equivalent mechanisms
- Session recordings conducted during Tenbound Blueprint engagements involving EU-based employees require explicit notification and consent per GDPR Article 6

**Impact on marketing:** Marketing materials targeting EU audiences must not imply that contact data can be used without a lawful basis. Claims about European data coverage must reference GDPR-compliant handling. The CIENCE Europe SDR tier and Cognism-competitive positioning must acknowledge GDPR as a design constraint, not just a feature.

### CCPA (California Consumer Privacy Act)
**Applies to:** Processing of personal data belonging to California residents; relevant to graph8 Platform data, visitor identification, and any CIENCE-managed campaigns targeting California-based contacts

**Requirements:**
- California residents have the right to know what personal data is collected and how it is used
- California residents have the right to opt out of the sale or sharing of their personal information
- A 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information' link or equivalent mechanism must be accessible
- Opt-out requests must be honored within 15 business days
- Data collected about California residents must be disclosed in graph8's and customers' privacy policies
- Customers using graph8's buyer graph data to target California residents must ensure their own CCPA compliance posture

**Impact on marketing:** graph8 marketing materials must reference Privacy Policy for CCPA-specific rights. Customer-facing materials on visitor identification and contact enrichment must note customer responsibility for CCPA compliance in their own deployments.

### TCPA (Telephone Consumer Protection Act)
**Applies to:** All outbound calling conducted via the graph8 Dialer (power dialer, parallel dialer), AI Voice Agents (inbound and outbound), and CIENCE SDR teams making calls to US-based numbers

**Requirements:**
- Prior express written consent is required before placing autodialed or prerecorded calls to cell phones
- Do-Not-Call (DNC) registry compliance: numbers on the National DNC Registry must be suppressed before calling
- Company-specific DNC lists must be maintained and honored
- Abandoned call rates for predictive/parallel dialing must not exceed FCC thresholds (currently 3% per 30-day period per campaign)
- Calls to cell phones using an automatic telephone dialing system (ATDS) without consent are prohibited
- AI Voice Agents placing outbound calls must comply with disclosure requirements if the call is AI-generated (see applicable state laws such as California AB 2188)

**Impact on marketing:** Marketing materials describing the graph8 Dialer, parallel dialing, and AI Voice Agent capabilities must note that customers are responsible for TCPA compliance, DNC scrubbing, and consent management. Claims like 'call anyone' or 'unlimited outbound calls' must not be used without qualifying language.

### CASL (Canada's Anti-Spam Legislation)
**Applies to:** All commercial electronic messages (email, SMS, LinkedIn messages) sent to Canadian recipients via graph8 Campaigns & Sequencer, AI Inbox, WhatsApp integration, and CIENCE-managed outbound campaigns

**Requirements:**
- Express or implied consent must be obtained before sending commercial electronic messages to Canadian recipients
- Every message must identify the sender and provide contact information
- Every message must include a functioning unsubscribe mechanism
- Unsubscribe requests must be honored within 10 business days
- Implied consent has a time limit (typically 2 years for business relationships) and must be tracked
- Purchasing or using third-party contact lists for Canadian recipients requires verification that the original consent obtained covers the type of message being sent

**Impact on marketing:** Canadian-market campaigns built in graph8 or executed by CIENCE must include CASL-compliant footers and consent tracking. Marketing materials must not suggest that B2B prospecting to Canadian contacts is consent-free.

### FTC Endorsement and Testimonial Guidelines (16 CFR Part 255)
**Applies to:** All customer testimonials, case studies, review platform ratings (G2, Clutch, Gartner Peer Insights, TrustRadius, UpCity, CrowdReviews, GoodFirms, Google), and influencer or partner endorsements used in graph8, CIENCE, and Tenbound marketing

**Requirements:**
- Material connections between graph8/CIENCE/Tenbound and any endorser must be clearly disclosed
- Testimonials must reflect the honest opinions of the endorser and must not be presented as typical results without substantiation
- If a client result is used as a testimonial, it must represent what customers can generally expect, or be clearly labeled as an atypical outcome
- Review platform aggregations (e.g., '4.4 avg. rating across 8 review platforms') must be accurate and current at time of publication
- AI-generated or AI-assisted testimonials (if any) must be disclosed

**Impact on marketing:** CIENCE's '4.4 avg. rating across 8 review platforms,' '2,500+ clients served,' and '115+ case studies' claims must be verifiable and current. Review scores cited in marketing must be updated regularly. Client logos and brand names used in CIENCE/Tenbound marketing (Okta, LinkedIn, GitLab, Gong, Outreach, Salesloft) must reflect documented engagements only.

### E-Sign Act (ESIGN) and UETA (Uniform Electronic Transactions Act)
**Applies to:** graph8 Platform - Quotes & E-Sign product and the quote-to-cash workflow within the Revenue (CRM) module

**Requirements:**
- Electronic signatures must be legally equivalent to handwritten signatures for contracts within ESIGN/UETA scope
- Signatories must have the ability to opt out of electronic signature and receive paper documents if requested
- Records of electronic signatures must be retained and reproducible for legal purposes
- The platform must be able to demonstrate that the electronic signature was applied by the intended signatory
- Automatic billing provisioning triggered by e-signature must not execute until a valid, verified e-signature is recorded

**Impact on marketing:** Marketing claims that graph8 Quotes & E-Sign 'replaces PandaDoc, DocuSign, and manual Stripe' must not overstate legal equivalency in jurisdictions where ESIGN/UETA does not apply (e.g., certain international markets). Marketing should direct customers to review their local e-signature laws.

### AI Transparency and Disclosure Laws (State and Emerging Federal)
**Applies to:** graph8 AI Voice Agents, AI Inbox auto-reply, AI agents (Chief of Staff, SDR Agent, RevOps Agent), Studio AI-generated content, and any AI-generated outreach sent from customer domains

**Requirements:**
- California AB 2188 and similar state laws may require disclosure when an AI is conducting a phone conversation; customers using AI Voice Agents for outbound calls must comply with applicable state disclosure requirements
- AI-generated emails and messages sent at scale may be subject to emerging FTC guidance on deceptive AI use; human-in-the-loop review for first-contact outreach is strongly recommended
- Customers must not use AI Voice Agents to impersonate humans in a way that deceives the called party upon request
- graph8's AI agent action log (audit trail) must be retained by customers as evidence of human oversight and control
- Any AI-generated content used in regulated industries (healthcare, financial services, legal) must be reviewed by a qualified human professional before use

**Impact on marketing:** Marketing for AI Voice Agents, AI Inbox, and AI Agents must include language about customer responsibility for disclosure compliance. Claims like 'sounds just like your rep' or 'indistinguishable from human' must include qualifying language about disclosure obligations.

## Approved Claims

### graph8's buyer graph contains 700M+ verified contacts and 100M+ companies.

**Evidence:**
- Stated on graph8.com/platform/data/ and graph8.com/pricing/
- Data is verified before delivery; records failing verification are flagged, not delivered
- Waterfall enrichment across multiple third-party providers maintains data freshness

✅ **Correct usage:** Search 700M+ verified B2B contacts and 100M+ companies free on graph8 — no credit card required.
❌ **Incorrect usage:** 'Access the world's most accurate B2B database' or '100% verified contact accuracy' — neither accuracy claim is substantiated.
**Expiration:** Review quarterly; update figure if platform data coverage changes

### graph8 captures approximately 2 billion signals daily across visitor, intent, hiring, job change, social, tech stack, and funding sources.

**Evidence:**
- Stated on graph8.com/platform/signals/
- Signal sources include: site visitors, search intent, forms, hiring posts, job changes, social listening on X, tech stack changes, and funding/news announcements
- Signals are resolved to real people on the buyer graph

✅ **Correct usage:** graph8 Signals captures ~2 billion buying signals daily and resolves each to a real person on your buyer graph.
❌ **Incorrect usage:** 'graph8 monitors every B2B buying signal in real time' — 'every' and 'real time' overstate coverage and latency guarantees.
**Expiration:** Review annually or upon material change to signal source partnerships

### CIENCE has worked with 2,500+ B2B teams across enterprise, software, finance, and services verticals.

**Evidence:**
- Stated on cience.com and cience.com/pricing/
- Named clients include Okta, Microsoft, Google, Uber, Salesforce, Segment, Airbnb, BetterHelp, Learning Ally, WEX, VeChain, Instapage, and others
- 115+ documented public case studies referenced on cience.com

✅ **Correct usage:** CIENCE has run GTM campaigns for 2,500+ B2B teams, including Okta, Salesforce, and Segment.
❌ **Incorrect usage:** 'CIENCE guarantees results for any B2B company' or 'CIENCE worked with every major enterprise' — neither is substantiated.
**Expiration:** Review and update client count and named logos quarterly

### CIENCE holds an average rating of 4.4 across 8 review platforms.

**Evidence:**
- Stated on cience.com with platform-specific ratings: UpCity 4.8, Clutch 4.4, CrowdReviews 4.8, GoodFirms 4.8, G2 4.0, TrustRadius 4.3, Google 4.0, Gartner Peer Insights 4.1
- Ratings are described as 'live, verified, and public'

✅ **Correct usage:** CIENCE holds a 4.4 average rating across 8 major review platforms, including G2, Clutch, and Gartner Peer Insights.
❌ **Incorrect usage:** 'CIENCE is the highest-rated lead generation service' — superlative claims require current, verified comparative data.
**Expiration:** Review platform scores monthly; update marketing materials within 30 days of material rating changes

### graph8 is built on a decade of real B2B outbound campaign data from CIENCE.

**Evidence:**
- Stated on graph8.com homepage and multiple platform product pages
- CIENCE has run millions of calls, emails, and meetings across thousands of B2B campaigns
- graph8 AI and scoring models are trained on CIENCE campaign outcomes, not generic internet data

✅ **Correct usage:** graph8's AI is trained on 10 years of real CIENCE outbound data — millions of conversations, calls, and campaign outcomes — not a generic model.
❌ **Incorrect usage:** 'graph8 AI is more accurate than any other AI sales platform' — comparative accuracy claims require substantiated benchmarking.
**Expiration:** Review annually; update tenure claim each year

### graph8 Team plan provides unlimited users with no per-seat fees at $99/month.

**Evidence:**
- Stated on graph8.com/pricing/
- Team plan explicitly includes: 'Unlimited users, no seat fees' and 'Invite everyone. Pricing never scales with headcount.'
- 10,000 execution credits included per month for the whole organization

✅ **Correct usage:** The graph8 Team plan is $99/month for your entire organization — unlimited users, no seat fees, with 10,000 execution credits included.
❌ **Incorrect usage:** 'graph8 is always free for unlimited users' — the free tier has credit limits; unlimited users is a Team plan feature.
**Expiration:** Review upon any pricing change

### The Tenbound Programmable Revenue Blueprint is $1,000 one-time with no vendor commitment on the other side.

**Evidence:**
- Stated on tenbound.com/pricing/
- Deliverables are owned by the client; Tenbound has no financial interest in post-engagement vendor selection
- Clients receive 5 documents: revenue ontology, integration gaps, maturity readout, setup document, and improvement proposal

✅ **Correct usage:** $1,000 one time. Three weeks. Five documents yours to keep and implement — with any vendor or in-house. No upsell on the other side.
❌ **Incorrect usage:** 'The Blueprint guarantees pipeline improvement' or 'Tenbound will fix your pipeline' — the Blueprint is an assessment and documentation service; implementation is the client's responsibility.
**Expiration:** Review upon any pricing or scope change

### graph8 Signals' visitor identification resolves anonymous site traffic to the company and individual level without requiring a form submission.

**Evidence:**
- Stated on graph8.com/platform/signals/
- Feature described as: 'Resolve traffic to company and person,' 'See the exact pages they viewed,' 'No form required to identify them'
- Results are written to the buyer graph and are immediately actionable

✅ **Correct usage:** graph8 Signals identifies the companies and people visiting your site — no form required — and flags high-intent visitors for immediate outreach.
❌ **Incorrect usage:** 'graph8 can identify every anonymous visitor' — identification rates vary by traffic source, browser, and network; 100% identification is not guaranteed.
**Expiration:** Review annually or upon material change to visitor ID technology

### The Tenbound Pipeline Architecture Standard is published, free to read, and grades pipeline systems against six pillars: Market, Signal, Message, Motion, Mastery, and Measurement.

**Evidence:**
- Stated on tenbound.com/standard/
- Standard is described as 'free to read, share, and build on' with attribution to Tenbound required
- The six pillars are defined with explicit break conditions, coverage areas, and maturity levels

✅ **Correct usage:** The Tenbound Pipeline Architecture Standard is free to read and use. Grade your pipeline against six pillars — Market, Signal, Message, Motion, Mastery, and Measurement — and find the constraint costing you the most.
❌ **Incorrect usage:** 'Tenbound's Standard is the industry-accepted benchmark for all B2B sales teams' — while the Standard is published and in use, no independent body has formally certified it as a universal industry standard.
**Expiration:** Review upon any update to the Standard's published content

### graph8's quote-to-cash workflow provisions Stripe billing automatically upon e-signature, replacing PandaDoc, DocuSign, and manual Stripe entry.

**Evidence:**
- Stated on graph8.com/platform/revenue/
- Workflow: quote built → sent for e-sign → signed → Stripe customer, subscription/invoice, and payment link provisioned automatically
- Described as 'one flow, not three tools re-keyed by hand'

✅ **Correct usage:** When your quote is signed in graph8, billing provisions itself in Stripe automatically — no manual re-keying, no separate doc tool.
❌ **Incorrect usage:** 'graph8 replaces your entire billing and finance stack' — graph8 provisions Stripe; it does not replace dedicated billing, accounting, or ERP systems.
**Expiration:** Review upon any change to Stripe integration or e-sign capabilities

## Forbidden Terms

### Legal Reasons
- ❌ **guaranteed results** - Marketing outcomes cannot be legally guaranteed; creates false expectations and potential liability for graph8.
- ❌ **100% accurate** - No data provider can claim perfect accuracy; applies to the graph8 Data product's 700M+ contact database and all enrichment outputs.
- ❌ **unlimited** - All platform tiers have usage limits (API calls, seats, credits); using 'unlimited' without qualification is misleading and legally risky.
- ❌ **best in class** - Superlative claim requiring substantiated third-party benchmarking; cannot be used without current, cited evidence.
- ❌ **#1** - Ranking claim requires verified, dated third-party source; forbidden without explicit legal-approved citation.
- ❌ **clone voices without consent** - AI Voice Agent voice-cloning features must only be described in contexts that imply lawful consent from the rep whose voice is cloned; implying otherwise creates legal and regulatory exposure.
- ❌ **scrape** - Implies unlawful or unauthorized data collection; all graph8 data is sourced from licensed and publicly available sources.
- ❌ **bypass GDPR** - Suggesting the platform enables circumvention of privacy regulations is false, illegal to imply, and directly contradicts graph8's data compliance standards.
- ❌ **free forever** - Any free tier or trial is subject to terms and limitations; 'free forever' creates contractual ambiguity and misleads prospects.
- ❌ **real-time (without qualification)** - Signal capture and data enrichment have processing latencies; 'real-time' must be qualified (e.g., 'near real-time') to be accurate for graph8 Signals and AI Inbox products.
- ❌ **HIPAA compliant** - graph8 does not currently hold a BAA-backed HIPAA certification; claiming compliance without documented certification is prohibited.

### Competitive Reasons
- ❌ **beat [competitor name]** - Disparaging competitor comparisons without substantiated, current, third-party validated benchmarks are legally and reputationally risky.

### Brand Reasons
- ❌ **spam** - Describing outbound email or SMS capabilities using this term undermines brand credibility and implies non-compliance with CAN-SPAM/TCPA.
- ❌ **hack** - Negative brand connotation and implies unauthorized system access, which conflicts with graph8's compliance-first positioning.
- ❌ **steal customers** - Implies unethical business practices; conflicts with graph8's professional B2B brand positioning.

## Competitor Mentions

**Can mention competitors:** Yes

**Rules:**
- All competitor mentions must be factually accurate and substantiated by current, third-party validated data or publicly available information.
- Competitor names may only be used in approved comparison contexts (e.g., G2 category pages, feature comparison tables reviewed by Legal).
- Do not use competitor logos, trademarked taglines, or brand assets without explicit written permission.
- Comparative claims must reflect the most recent product capabilities of both graph8 and the competitor; outdated comparisons must be retired within 30 days of a competitor's material product update.
- All competitor-comparative content must be reviewed and approved by Legal and Marketing leadership before publication.
- Avoid emotionally charged or disparaging language when referencing competitors; maintain a professional, factual tone.
- Do not imply that competitors engage in unethical, illegal, or deceptive practices unless supported by verified public legal records.

**Approved comparisons:**
- ✅ Feature-for-feature comparison tables (e.g., graph8 Platform vs. ZoomInfo on data coverage, intent signals, and AI automation) when backed by current public documentation or third-party reviews.
- ✅ Category positioning statements referencing analyst reports (e.g., G2 Grid rankings, Forrester Wave) citing graph8 alongside named competitors.
- ✅ Pricing transparency comparisons where competitor pricing is publicly listed and accurately represented.
- ✅ Customer-sourced testimonials referencing a switch from a competitor, provided the customer has given written approval for the quote.

**Forbidden comparisons:**
- ❌ Claiming graph8 is 'better than' a specific competitor without cited, date-stamped, third-party benchmark data.
- ❌ Using a competitor's name in paid search ad copy in a manner that violates that competitor's trademark policies or platform ad guidelines.
- ❌ Implying a competitor's product is insecure, non-compliant, or inferior in data ethics without verified public evidence.
- ❌ Fabricating or extrapolating competitor feature gaps not confirmed by their current public documentation.
- ❌ Side-by-side pricing comparisons using estimated or unverified competitor pricing.

## Review Process

### Always Review
- All content making performance or ROI claims (e.g., 'increase pipeline by X%')
- Any content referencing competitor names, products, or pricing
- Press releases and earned media pitches
- Paid advertising copy across all channels (Google, LinkedIn, Meta, programmatic)
- Email campaign templates deployed via graph8 Campaigns & Sequencer to external prospects
- AI Voice Agent scripts used for outbound calling campaigns
- Case studies and customer success stories citing specific metrics
- Product pages referencing data coverage claims (e.g., 700M+ contacts, 2B signals/day)
- Any content referencing regulatory compliance (GDPR, CCPA, CAN-SPAM, TCPA)
- SMS and WhatsApp campaign copy due to TCPA and international messaging regulations
- Pricing pages and packaging descriptions
- Partner and co-marketing materials

### No Review Needed
- Internal Slack messages and team communications
- Internal training documents not published externally
- Social media posts sharing already-approved blog content without modification
- Direct replies to inbound customer support queries using approved response templates
- Personal LinkedIn posts by employees that do not reference specific graph8 product claims or metrics

### Process
**Submit to:** legal-marketing-review@graph8.com
**Timeline:** 5 business days for standard review; submissions received after 3pm local time are processed the following business day.
**Expedited:** 48-hour expedited review available for time-sensitive launches; must be requested via legal-marketing-review@graph8.com with subject line 'EXPEDITED REQUEST' and executive sponsor approval attached.

**Approval required from:**
- Legal / Compliance Team
- VP of Marketing or CMO
- Product Marketing (for all product capability claims)
- Sales Leadership (for outbound campaign templates and dialer scripts)

## Penalties

### Regulatory Penalties
- **GDPR:** Fines of up to €20 million or 4% of annual global turnover, whichever is higher, for violations involving unlawful processing of EU personal data.
- **CCPA:** Civil penalties of up to $7,500 per intentional violation and $2,500 per unintentional violation enforced by the California Attorney General.
- **CAN-SPAM:** Penalties of up to $51,744 per individual non-compliant commercial email message.
- **TCPA:** Statutory damages of $500–$1,500 per unsolicited SMS or call; class action exposure for bulk outbound campaigns via graph8 Dialer and Campaigns.
- **FTC Act (Section 5):** FTC enforcement actions for deceptive advertising claims, including consent orders, fines, and required corrective advertising.

### Company Policy
- First violation (unintentional): Written warning issued to the responsible team member and their manager; mandatory compliance re-training within 5 business days.
- Second violation or first intentional violation: Formal disciplinary action per HR policy, potential removal of content publishing permissions, and mandatory Legal review of all future content for 90 days.
- Third violation or willful disregard of compliance rules: Escalation to executive leadership; potential termination of employment or contractor agreement in accordance with company policy.
- Any content published without required Legal approval must be taken down within 2 hours of discovery; incident report filed with Legal within 24 hours.
- Agency or contractor partners found in violation will receive a cure notice; repeated violations may result in contract termination.
- Violations involving competitor disparagement or false advertising claims will be escalated immediately to Legal for assessment of third-party legal exposure.

# Style Guide

## Portfolio scope: graph8, CIENCE, and Tenbound

Visual scope includes graph8, CIENCE, and Tenbound as distinct identities. Use graph8 assets for platform communications, CIENCE assets for managed-service communications, and Tenbound assets for assessment, research, standards, and maturity-model content. A Tenbound Blueprint or framework page should clearly carry Tenbound attribution and its own approved assets. Shared portfolio context does not justify replacing Tenbound's identity with the graph8 logo or describing its framework as a software feature.

---

# Style Guide

**Design Philosophy:** LIGHT-FIRST design system. The graph8 portfolio (graph8 platform, CIENCE managed services, Tenbound research institute) is built on a warm parchment canvas (#F2EFE9) — not clinical white — creating an editorial, revenue-engineering aesthetic that signals craftsmanship over commodity SaaS. The primary brand color is a vivid electric violet (#7D2DF3), commanding attention as the dominant UI anchor for interactive elements, links, and primary actions. The deep aubergine-plum (#251B3A) serves as the secondary dark surface, while the muted burgundy-plum (#461B3C) governs interactive link text. Typography is set exclusively in Aeonik — a geometric sans-serif with sharp, rational letterforms — for both headings (76px → 57.6px scale) and body (17px), maintaining single-typeface discipline across the entire system. A monospace stack (SF Mono / JetBrains Mono / Roboto Mono) handles code, CLI commands, credit values, and data outputs, drawing a hard visual boundary between prose and machine output. Primary buttons are sharply square-cornered (0px radius), borrowing from print and editorial traditions to communicate directness and operational confidence. Input fields carry 8px radius, creating a deliberate hierarchy between data entry surfaces and action triggers. The overall system reads as a revenue-engineering platform — precise, uncluttered, and built for operators who have been oversold by generic SaaS aesthetics. Each of the three brands (graph8, CIENCE, Tenbound) maintains distinct identity while sharing this foundational visual language.

## Key Principles

- Warm parchment canvas — not white: The site background (#F2EFE9) is a warm off-white that reduces eye strain and signals craftsmanship. Every surface decision defers to this warm-neutral foundation rather than clinical white or dark-mode defaults.
- Electric violet authority: The primary brand color (#7D2DF3) is a vivid, high-energy violet that commands attention without the ubiquitous enterprise blue. It is used for primary brand elements, interactive accents, and dominant UI anchors — differentiating graph8 from every incumbent in the GTM stack category.
- Deep plum depth: The secondary color (#251B3A) is a near-black aubergine-plum that anchors dark text, secondary containers, and structural UI elements — providing gravitas without defaulting to pure black.
- Editorial square corners on actions: Primary buttons carry 0px border radius — a sharp, architectural choice aligned with print-editorial design traditions, communicating zero tolerance for softness or ambiguity in execution-oriented UI.
- Monospace as data language: SF Mono, JetBrains Mono, and Roboto Mono are reserved for code, CLI commands, credit values, terminal-adjacent UI patterns, and data outputs — creating a clear visual register between prose and machine output.
- Single typeface discipline: Aeonik governs both headings (76px → 57.6px scale) and body (17px), creating typographic unity and preventing the visual noise of mixed typeface systems common in rushed SaaS design.
- Execution-first information architecture: Content is structured as numbered, progressive sections (01 /, 02 /, 03 /) that mirror the platform's sequential signal-to-revenue loop — design structure reinforces product logic across all three brands.

## Color Palette

**Primary Colors:**
- {'name': 'Electric Violet', 'hex_code': '#7D2DF3', 'rgb': 'rgb(125, 45, 243)', 'usage': 'Primary brand color for interactive elements, CTA highlights, primary brand anchors, links within the app interface, and dominant hero accents. Conveys energy, innovation, and sharp differentiation from the generic enterprise blue category.', 'accessibility_notes': 'Use white (#FFFFFF or #FCFCFC) text on this color. Verify contrast on #F2EFE9 backgrounds — may require pairing with white overlays for WCAG AA compliance on parchment surfaces.'}
- {'name': 'Warm Parchment', 'hex_code': '#F2EFE9', 'rgb': 'rgb(242, 239, 233)', 'usage': 'Primary page background (main canvas), primary button background fill, and accent surface. The warm off-white that defines the light-first aesthetic across graph8, CIENCE, and Tenbound. Also used as button fill on the primary CTA button component.', 'accessibility_notes': 'Light surface — always pair with #251B3A, #7D2DF3, #16140F, or #461B3C foreground colors to meet WCAG AA contrast requirements. Never place light gray text on this background.'}
- {'name': 'Aubergine Plum', 'hex_code': '#251B3A', 'rgb': 'rgb(37, 27, 58)', 'usage': 'Secondary brand color. Used for dark text blocks, secondary UI containers, structural headings, and near-black surfaces where pure black would feel too stark. Reads as deep navy-plum — authoritative and on-palette.', 'accessibility_notes': 'Excellent contrast on #F2EFE9 background (>7:1 ratio). Safe for WCAG AAA compliance on parchment surfaces. Use white text when this is used as a background fill.'}

**Secondary Colors:**
- {'name': 'Burgundy Link', 'hex_code': '#461B3C', 'rgb': 'rgb(70, 27, 60)', 'usage': 'All interactive hyperlink text and navigation link states. A deep plum-burgundy that reads as near-black while remaining on-palette. Distinguishes link text from body copy without introducing an out-of-palette blue.', 'accessibility_notes': 'Meets WCAG AA on #F2EFE9 parchment background. Do not use on dark backgrounds without verifying contrast. Pair with underline on hover for accessibility.'}
- {'name': 'Near Black Ink', 'hex_code': '#16140F', 'rgb': 'rgb(22, 20, 15)', 'usage': 'Primary button text color, input field text, and high-emphasis body content where maximum legibility is required. A warm near-black with slight brown undertone that stays on-palette with the parchment canvas.', 'accessibility_notes': 'Maximum contrast on #F2EFE9 (>12:1). Use for all body text, button labels, and form field content.'}
- {'name': 'Dark UI Surface', 'hex_code': '#171717', 'rgb': 'rgb(23, 23, 23)', 'usage': 'Secondary button background. Used for dark-mode UI elements within the otherwise light-first interface — particularly the secondary button component which inverts to dark fill with light text. Creates strong visual contrast against the parchment canvas.', 'accessibility_notes': 'Use #FCFCFC text on this background. Contrast is WCAG AAA compliant.'}

**Accent Colors:**
- {'name': 'Parchment Accent', 'hex_code': '#F2EFE9', 'rgb': 'rgb(242, 239, 233)', 'usage': 'Accent surface — used for highlighted regions, selected states, and warm background washes on cards or callout blocks that need to stand apart from the base canvas without introducing a new color. Doubles as the primary button background fill.', 'accessibility_notes': 'Same as primary background — ensure foreground text meets WCAG AA minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio.'}
- {'name': 'Pure White', 'hex_code': '#FFFFFF', 'rgb': 'rgb(255, 255, 255)', 'usage': 'Input field backgrounds, modal surfaces, and elevated card surfaces where a clean white is needed to contrast against the parchment canvas. Provides a clear visual lift for interactive data entry components.', 'accessibility_notes': 'Use #16140F or #030302 text on white surfaces. High contrast, WCAG AAA.'}
- {'name': 'Border Near-Black', 'hex_code': '#030302', 'rgb': 'rgb(3, 3, 2)', 'usage': 'Input field border color. The sharpest, most definitive border treatment — used on form inputs to create a crisp, precise boundary that signals data-entry precision in a revenue operations tool.', 'accessibility_notes': 'Maximum contrast. Use only as a border or stroke, not as body text background.'}
- {'name': 'Secondary Button Border', 'hex_code': '#292929', 'rgb': 'rgb(41, 41, 41)', 'usage': 'Border treatment for secondary (dark) buttons. Creates a subtle separation between the dark button surface and adjacent dark surfaces when buttons appear in dark UI regions.', 'accessibility_notes': 'Use only as a border/stroke on dark surfaces.'}

**Neutral Colors:**
- {'name': 'Mid Gray Body', 'hex_code': '#737373', 'rgb': 'rgb(115, 115, 115)', 'usage': 'Primary body text color for paragraph content, descriptive copy, and secondary information. A neutral mid-gray that provides comfortable reading contrast on the parchment canvas without the harshness of near-black for long-form content.', 'accessibility_notes': 'Meets WCAG AA (4.5:1) on #F2EFE9 parchment background for normal text at 17px. Verify at smaller sizes. Do not use for small UI labels under 14px.'}
- {'name': 'Near-White Text', 'hex_code': '#FCFCFC', 'rgb': 'rgb(252, 252, 252)', 'usage': 'Text color on dark surfaces — specifically the secondary button (dark background). Provides maximum legibility on #171717 button backgrounds without the clinical flatness of pure white.', 'accessibility_notes': 'WCAG AAA on #171717 dark button background. Safe for all text sizes.'}
- {'name': 'Light Border', 'hex_code': '#D3D0CA', 'rgb': 'rgb(211, 208, 202)', 'usage': 'Subtle dividers, secondary button borders in light contexts, and gentle card/section separators where a heavy border would disrupt the editorial flow of the parchment-first layout.', 'accessibility_notes': 'Use only as a non-text border or decorative separator, not as text or interactive element foreground.'}


## Typography

**Primary Font:**
  - Name: Aeonik
  - Category: Heading
  - Weights: ['400', '500', '600', '700']
  - Usage: All headings (H1 through H3), hero text, section titles, navigation labels, button labels, and any display-weight copy. Aeonik is a geometric sans-serif with sharp, rational letterforms and precise stroke contrast — it reads as technical and authoritative at large scales while remaining warm and accessible at body sizes. This is the sole display and heading typeface across the entire graph8, CIENCE, and Tenbound portfolio.
  - Fallback: system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif

**Secondary Font:**
  - Name: Aeonik
  - Category: Body
  - Weights: ['400', '500']
  - Usage: All body copy, paragraph text, captions, form labels, navigation sub-items, and UI prose. The same Aeonik family governs body text — a deliberate single-typeface discipline that creates system-wide typographic unity. At 17px/400 weight, Aeonik reads cleanly on the parchment canvas at comfortable line lengths for revenue leaders and operators consuming dense product documentation.
  - Fallback: system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif

**Additional Fonts:**
- {'name': 'SF Mono', 'category': 'Monospace', 'weights': ['400', '500'], 'usage': 'Code snippets, CLI command examples, API responses, credit values, execution counters, data field values, and any terminal-adjacent UI pattern. Reserved exclusively for machine output — creates a hard visual register boundary between prose and system data. Used on macOS/iOS rendering contexts.', 'fallback': "JetBrains Mono, Roboto Mono, 'Courier New', monospace"}
- {'name': 'JetBrains Mono', 'category': 'Monospace', 'weights': ['400', '500'], 'usage': 'Primary cross-platform monospace for developer-facing surfaces: MCP server documentation, CLI usage examples, API reference, code blocks in Studio output, and in-app terminal views. Renders with excellent ligature support and consistent metrics across operating systems.', 'fallback': "SF Mono, Roboto Mono, 'Courier New', monospace"}
- {'name': 'Roboto Mono', 'category': 'Monospace', 'weights': ['400', '500'], 'usage': 'Fallback monospace for Windows and Android rendering contexts. Used in the same patterns as SF Mono and JetBrains Mono — code, CLI, credits, data outputs. Ensures monospace discipline holds across all rendering environments.', 'fallback': "SF Mono, JetBrains Mono, 'Courier New', monospace"}

**Hierarchy:**
- H1: 76px / 700 weight / Aeonik — Hero headlines, page titles, major landing page statements. Used for primary value proposition text ('One buyer graph. Signal to revenue.'). Line height: 1.05. Letter spacing: -0.02em.
- H2: 57.6px / 600 weight / Aeonik — Section headings, major feature titles, pricing tier names. Line height: 1.1. Letter spacing: -0.015em.
- H3: 36px / 600 weight / Aeonik — Sub-section headings, feature group titles, card headlines. Line height: 1.2. Letter spacing: -0.01em.
- H4: 24px / 600 weight / Aeonik — Component headings, sidebar titles, table headers, numbered section openers (01 /, 02 /, 03 /). Line height: 1.3.
- Body: 17px / 400 weight / Aeonik — Primary paragraph text, feature descriptions, UI prose. Line height: 1.6. Color: #737373 on parchment canvas.
- Body Strong: 17px / 500 weight / Aeonik — Emphasized body phrases, inline highlights, key claims within paragraphs. Same size as body, weight bump for stress.
- Small / Caption: 14px / 400 weight / Aeonik — Metadata, timestamps, form helper text, tags, badges. Line height: 1.4.
- Monospace: 14px / 400 weight / SF Mono, JetBrains Mono, Roboto Mono — All code, CLI, credit counters, API values. Line height: 1.5. Color: #251B3A on parchment.

**Sizing Scale:**
  - Base Unit: 4px
  - Scale: 4 / 8 / 12 / 16 / 24 / 32 / 48 / 64 / 96 / 128
  - Note: All spacing, padding, margin, and layout dimensions derived from the 4px base unit. Components snap to this grid. The 8px border-radius on inputs and secondary buttons is a direct 2× base-unit application.


## Logo Usage

**Primary Logo:** The graph8 wordmark logo. SVG format. URL: https://graph8.com/img/graph8-logo.svg. The logo renders in the site header and links to the homepage root (/). The logotype uses the Aeonik typeface family consistent with the system-wide typography. The favicon companion is an SVG mark at https://graph8.com/favicon-g8.svg. CIENCE brand logo: https://www.cience.com/img/cience-black.svg (black wordmark on parchment/light surfaces). Tenbound brand logo: https://tenbound.com/img/logo-black.svg (black wordmark on parchment/light surfaces). OG social image: https://tenbound.com/og/graph8.png. Each brand maintains a fully separate logo asset — do not composite or combine the graph8, CIENCE, and Tenbound logos into a single lockup.
**Variations:**
- graph8 full wordmark — horizontal (primary): https://graph8.com/img/graph8-logo.svg
- graph8 favicon/icon mark (g8 symbol): https://graph8.com/favicon-g8.svg
- CIENCE wordmark (black, for light surfaces): https://www.cience.com/img/cience-black.svg
- Tenbound wordmark (black, for light surfaces): https://tenbound.com/img/logo-black.svg
- graph8 OG social card image: https://tenbound.com/og/graph8.png
- CIENCE OG social card image: https://tenbound.com/og/cience.png
- Tenbound OG social card image: https://tenbound.com/og/index.png

**Minimum Size:** 48px wide for the graph8 wordmark in digital contexts. The favicon mark (g8 symbol) minimum: 16px × 16px for browser favicon; 32px for UI icon contexts. CIENCE and Tenbound logos: minimum 48px wide. Below these sizes, switch to the standalone letterform mark or favicon asset.
**Clear Space:** Minimum clear space equal to the cap-height of the logotype on all four sides. For the graph8 wordmark at standard sizes, this is approximately 16px clearance on all sides. For the favicon/icon mark, maintain 4px clear space at minimum. CIENCE and Tenbound logos follow the same cap-height rule.
**Dont Rules:**
- Do not stretch, skew, or distort the logo proportions in any dimension.
- Do not recolor the graph8, CIENCE, or Tenbound logos — use only the approved SVG assets on appropriate backgrounds.
- Do not place the graph8 logo on a background with insufficient contrast — the wordmark requires at minimum a parchment (#F2EFE9), white (#FFFFFF), or dark (#251B3A / #171717) surface.
- Do not combine the graph8, CIENCE, and Tenbound logos into a single composite lockup — each brand maintains independent logo sovereignty.
- Do not use rasterized or low-resolution versions of the SVG logo assets in any digital context.
- Do not add drop shadows, glows, gradients, or visual effects to any of the three brand logos.
- Do not rotate the logo — horizontal orientation only for all three brand wordmarks.
- Do not use the CIENCE or Tenbound logos to represent graph8 platform products, and vice versa — attribute each logo only to its respective brand offering.

**Background Rules:** The graph8 wordmark (black/dark version) is optimized for use on the parchment canvas (#F2EFE9) or white (#FFFFFF) backgrounds. A white/light version may be used on dark surfaces (#251B3A, #171717). The CIENCE logo (cience-black.svg) is designed for light/parchment backgrounds. The Tenbound logo (logo-black.svg) is designed for light/parchment backgrounds. For co-branded surfaces where all three brands appear together, maintain the parchment (#F2EFE9) background with each wordmark rendered in its approved dark version, separated by adequate white space and a thin divider.

## Imagery Guidelines

**Style:** Clean, editorial photography and precision-crafted UI mockery screens. The visual tone is operator-grade — showing real product interfaces (My Desk, Team HQ, pipeline kanban, signal streams) rendered with sharp fidelity rather than abstract gradients or lifestyle photography. Photography, when used, favors uncluttered environments: a single person at a desk, a focused team in a working session, a revenue leader reviewing data — never stock-photography cheerfulness or posed group shots. The overall aesthetic is purposeful and professional, consistent with the parchment-and-violet palette.
**Subjects:**
- Authentic product UI screens: the graph8 platform interface showing real features — My Desk ranked action queue, pipeline kanban boards, signal stream dashboards, Team HQ leaderboards, Studio context documents
- Revenue professionals at work: SDRs on calls, AEs reviewing deal cards, RevOps leaders analyzing pipeline data — real working contexts, not staged demos
- Data and precision visual metaphors: graphs resolving to people, signal streams converging, buyer graph network visualizations rendered in the electric violet and aubergine palette
- Engineering and assessment contexts for Tenbound: whiteboards, session recordings, maturity model diagrams, six-pillar framework illustrations — communicating rigor and methodology
- Team collaboration scenes: small groups in a shared workspace or remote-first setups where screens show real tools — not generic tech office stock photography

**Treatments:**
- Parchment wash overlay (#F2EFE9 at 10–20% opacity) on photography to tie images to the warm canvas palette
- Electric violet (#7D2DF3) accent lines, borders, or highlight treatments on UI screen captures to draw attention to key interface elements
- High-contrast monochrome treatment for editorial black-and-white photography used in Tenbound research and thought leadership contexts
- No heavy filters, vignettes, or Instagram-style color grading — images should read as accurate and trustworthy, not dramatized
- UI screens rendered at exact pixel dimensions from actual product — no approximation or fictional interface states in published materials

**Avoid:**
- Generic stock photography of smiling businesspeople shaking hands or pointing at whiteboards
- Abstract blurred light bokeh backgrounds or colorful gradient mesh imagery that reads as undifferentiated SaaS
- Imagery with primary colors outside the brand palette (no bright reds, electric blues, or lime greens as dominant image tones)
- Clip art, icon-as-illustration styles, or cartoon/illustrated characters as primary visual elements
- Dark, moody photography inconsistent with the light-first parchment canvas — the system is explicitly LIGHT-FIRST
- Photography showing competitor logos, competitor product interfaces, or out-of-category technology contexts
- Staged team photos where participants are clearly not doing real revenue work


## Iconography

**Style:** Outline
**Stroke Weight:** 1.5px at 20–24px sizes; 1px at 16px; 2px at 32–48px. Stroke weight scales with icon size to maintain visual consistency at different display densities.
**Sizing:** 16px (small / inline), 20px (default UI), 24px (medium / feature icons), 32px (large / section icons), 48px (hero / illustration icons). All icon sizes snap to the 4px base unit grid. The 20px default size is used for navigation, button-adjacent icons, and inline UI controls.
**Usage Rules:**
- Use outline (stroke) icons exclusively — do not mix filled and outline styles within the same UI surface.
- Icons must be rendered in the same color as their parent text element or in the designated UI color for the context (#251B3A for default UI, #7D2DF3 for highlighted/active states, #737373 for secondary/inactive states).
- Do not apply color fills to icon interiors unless the icon is in a selected/active state, where a light #7D2DF3 fill at 10% opacity may indicate selection.
- Icon touch targets must be a minimum of 44×44px for interactive icons regardless of the rendered icon size — use padding to achieve this.
- Monospace/terminal contexts (CLI, MCP server, code blocks) may use ASCII or Unicode character-based indicators instead of SVG icons to reinforce the machine-output visual register.
- For the three-brand portfolio: use consistent icon language across graph8, CIENCE, and Tenbound surfaces. Icons for pipeline pillars (Market, Signal, Message, Motion, Mastery, Measurement) should be a defined and reused set across all Tenbound-branded materials.
- Icon labels: always accompany icons with a visible or screen-reader-accessible text label in interactive contexts. Icons alone are insufficient for primary navigation or action triggers.


## Layout Guidelines

**Grid System:** 12-column responsive grid. Desktop (1280px+): 12 columns, 24px gutters, 80px outer margins. Laptop (1024px–1279px): 12 columns, 20px gutters, 48px outer margins. Tablet (768px–1023px): 8 columns, 16px gutters, 32px outer margins. Mobile (320px–767px): 4 columns, 16px gutters, 16px outer margins. The graph8 platform uses a numbered section architecture (01 /, 02 /, 03 /) as the primary page structure — each major section is a full-width band with constrained content width (max 1200px centered). Marketing pages use a centered single-column or two-column layout on desktop; the app interface uses a persistent left navigation sidebar (240px fixed) with a fluid main content area.
**Spacing Scale:** 4px base unit. Scale: 4 / 8 / 12 / 16 / 24 / 32 / 48 / 64 / 96 / 128px. Component internal padding: 12–16px for compact components (buttons, tags, badges), 24px for cards and panels, 32–48px for section padding. Section vertical rhythm uses 64px (between major page sections) and 96–128px (between hero and first content section).
**Margins:** 80px outer margin on desktop (1280px+ viewports). 48px on laptop. 32px on tablet. 16px on mobile. Content max-width: 1200px centered. Prose/reading content max-width: 720px centered within the 12-column grid to maintain comfortable 60–80 character line lengths at 17px body text.
**Alignment Rules:**
- Left-align all body copy and UI content — center alignment is reserved for hero headlines and isolated CTA sections only.
- The numbered section pattern (01 /, 02 /, 03 /) uses a consistent left-aligned number label in a smaller weight, with the section headline immediately following on the same or next line.
- Card grids use equal-width columns with consistent gutters — no orphaned single cards on a row in 3-column layouts; collapse to 2-column or 1-column at appropriate breakpoints.
- Form elements (inputs, selects, textareas) align to a consistent left edge within their container with full-width layout on mobile.
- Navigation: the primary nav is left-aligned in the header with the logo on the far left. CTAs ('Start Free', 'Book a meeting') are right-aligned in the nav bar.
- Table data: left-align text columns, right-align numeric columns (pricing, credits, percentages). Use monospace font for all numeric table values.


**Motion Guidelines:** Transitions: 150–200ms ease-out for all micro-interactions (hover states, focus rings, button presses, dropdown reveals). Use 200ms for elements entering the viewport and 150ms for elements leaving. Page-level transitions: fade-in with 240ms ease-out and a 4px upward translate (translateY(4px) → translateY(0)) for major content sections loading. Hover states on buttons: subtle background shift (no scale transform) — primary button darkens border from #16140F to #251B3A at 150ms; secondary button lightens background from #171717 to #292929 at 150ms. Agent activity indicators (the live feed in Team HQ, signal stream updates, My Desk card ranking): use a 300ms ease-in-out fade for new item appearance, never instant pop-in. Approval/action modals: slide up from bottom on mobile (300ms cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)), fade in centered on desktop (200ms ease-out). Leaderboard position changes: 400ms ease-in-out vertical translate to communicate rank movement clearly without being distracting. Loading states: use a pulsing opacity animation (0.4 → 1 → 0.4) at 1.2s duration on skeleton screens — do not use spinning loaders except for determinate progress. Avoid: parallax effects, large-scale transforms, bounce easings, or any animation exceeding 500ms in duration. The system is built for operators, not consumers — motion serves clarity, never spectacle.
