# Writing Style Guide

## Portfolio scope: graph8, CIENCE, and Tenbound

This writing guide covers graph8 software, CIENCE managed services, and Tenbound assessment and research. For Tenbound, use the exact names Pipeline Architecture Standard, Sales Pipeline Maturity Model, and Programmable Revenue Blueprint. Explain assessment terms such as revenue ontology before using them; distinguish published frameworks from findings about a particular customer. Tenbound content should guide a diagnostic decision, with an assessment or research CTA rather than an unrelated platform CTA.

---

# Writing Style Guide

**Purpose:** This guide defines how graph8, CIENCE, and Tenbound write across all communications — from marketing copy and product interfaces to AI-generated content and system messages. It ensures consistency, clarity, and brand alignment across the full portfolio, grounded in patterns extracted directly from live website content.

## Core Principles

- Say the thing directly. Every sentence earns its place. The sites use fragments intentionally: 'Three weeks. One engineer inside your team. One blueprint you keep.' Cut every word that does not add meaning.
- Write for the person doing the work, not the decision tree. Address revenue leaders, sales reps, and operators by their actual job context — 'whoever runs outbound,' 'your AE,' 'the rep on the call' — not abstract buyer personas.
- Name the problem before naming the solution. Every major section opens with what is broken: 'Your data is scattered, stale, and rented.' The fix only lands after the reader recognizes their situation.
- Show the system, not just the feature. Describe how things connect end to end — signal to cash, week one to week three, manual to autonomous. Isolated feature claims are avoided; the loop and the outcome always follow.
- Be honest about what you do and do not do. Tenbound says 'no vendor on the other side of the plan' and 'we say so' when a team scores high. CIENCE lists commission math in full. Transparency is a deliberate style choice, not a legal disclaimer.

## Tone Voice

**Voice Summary:** graph8, CIENCE, and Tenbound write with the confidence of a practitioner who has run the motion before — direct, specific, and unsentimental. The voice is never casual-breezy or corporate-stiff; it sits in the register of a forward-deployed engineer explaining the work to someone who owns a number. Sentences are short. Fragments are common and intentional. The reader is treated as intelligent and busy, so context is given fast and filler is cut. Warmth shows up as honesty — telling the buyer when something will not work for them, giving the economics in full, naming the constraint before pitching the fix. Metaphors are functional, not decorative. The brand sounds like it has seen the inside of a lot of sales orgs and is not trying to impress anyone.
**Attributes:**
- {'attribute': 'Direct', 'what_it_means': 'Say exactly what something does or costs in the fewest possible words. No hedging, no preamble.', 'sounds_like': "Lead with the action or the number. Cut 'we are pleased to offer' and 'leverage.' Write 'An engineer sits with your team for 45 minutes per role' not 'Our solution enables deep discovery engagement.'", 'do_example': 'Pay for what graph8 executes. Unlimited users on the Team plan.', 'dont_example': "Our flexible, scalable pricing model is designed to align with your team's unique growth objectives."}
- {'attribute': 'Practitioner-credible', 'what_it_means': 'Claims land because they are grounded in specific, verifiable detail — campaign counts, client names, time frames, dollar figures.', 'sounds_like': "Anchor every claim to a real number or named reference. 'Fifty three companies are on our client record, Okta, LinkedIn, GitLab, Gong, Outreach and Salesloft among them.' Not vague social proof.", 'do_example': 'Built on a decade of real CIENCE outbound across thousands of B2B campaigns, not a generic model.', 'dont_example': 'Trusted by leading B2B companies around the world to drive results.'}
- {'attribute': 'Honest', 'what_it_means': 'The copy acknowledges what the product does not do, when a program is not the right fit, and where the reader will have to do work themselves.', 'sounds_like': "Use 'not yet if' lists, explicit commission math, and 'no vendor on the other side of the plan.' Name failure modes, not just success states.", 'do_example': 'Not yet if: You want a guaranteed meeting number before anyone records a baseline. Nobody can show the workflow on a screen.', 'dont_example': 'Our proven system delivers guaranteed results for teams of all sizes and maturity levels.'}
- {'attribute': 'Precise', 'what_it_means': 'Specific over general at every turn. Exact time frames, exact prices, exact role names, exact step counts.', 'sounds_like': "Name the role ('SDR, AE, sales manager, growth, marketing'), the duration ('45 minutes each'), the output ('five documents'), the price ('$1,000'). Avoid 'some,' 'many,' 'various,' 'robust.'", 'do_example': 'Three weeks, up to 7 roles, one FDE. Yours to implement. No vendor on the other side of the plan.', 'dont_example': 'Our comprehensive engagement involves multiple stakeholders over a period of several weeks.'}
- {'attribute': 'Calm-authoritative', 'what_it_means': 'Confident without hype. No exclamation points on claims. No superlatives unless they are backed by a cited source.', 'sounds_like': "State the fact. Let the number or the outcome carry the weight. 'When northwind closes, the whole floor sees it' not 'Incredible win notifications!'", 'do_example': 'graph8 senses who is in-market, opens a launch, runs the outreach and conversations, builds pipeline, closes revenue, and learns from the outcome. Then it does it again, sharper.', 'dont_example': 'Supercharge your pipeline with our amazing AI-powered revenue engine!'}

**Always Do:**
- Use second person ('you,' 'your team,' 'your reps') to keep the reader in the scene.
- Lead section intros with the problem the reader already feels, then introduce the solution.
- Use numerals for all prices, credit counts, time frames, and metrics — never spell them out in body copy.
- Write CTAs as verb-first actions specific to the outcome: 'Start Free,' 'Book a meeting,' 'Buy now,' 'Join Demo.'
- Use fragment sentences for emphasis and rhythm, especially in headlines and feature callouts.

**Never Do:**
- Use exclamation points in marketing copy or product UI.
- Use superlatives without a cited source ('best,' 'leading,' 'most powerful').
- Use passive voice when an active agent can own the action.
- Write 'leverage,' 'synergy,' 'robust,' 'seamless,' 'cutting-edge,' or similar B2B filler.
- Promise outcomes that depend on the customer's own execution without naming that dependency.


## Capitalization

**Rules:**
- {'category': 'Company name — graph8', 'rule': "Always lowercase, even at the start of a sentence or headline. The brand name is 'graph8' in all contexts.", 'example_correct': 'graph8 finds buyers and runs the outreach.', 'example_incorrect': 'Graph8 finds buyers and runs the outreach.'}
- {'category': 'Company name — CIENCE', 'rule': "Always all-caps: CIENCE. Never 'Cience' or 'cience.'", 'example_correct': 'CIENCE pricing starts with a one-time GTM setup sprint.', 'example_incorrect': 'Cience pricing starts with a one-time GTM setup sprint.'}
- {'category': 'Company name — Tenbound', 'rule': 'Title case: Tenbound. Capital T, lowercase b.', 'example_correct': 'Buy it on tenbound.com. Tenbound benchmarks, frameworks, and research.', 'example_incorrect': 'TENBOUND benchmarks, frameworks, and research.'}
- {'category': 'Named platform features', 'rule': 'Title case for named product surfaces and agents: My Desk, Chief of Staff, SDR Agent, RevOps Agent, Team HQ, Studio, Buyer Graph, AE Cockpit.', 'example_correct': 'My Desk ranks every card by urgency and deal value.', 'example_incorrect': 'My desk ranks every card by urgency and deal value.'}
- {'category': 'Generic feature descriptors', 'rule': "Lowercase when describing a feature generically rather than naming it as a product surface: 'the sequencer,' 'the dialer,' 'the inbox.'", 'example_correct': 'The 5-channel sequencer runs email, phone, LinkedIn, SMS, and WhatsApp.', 'example_incorrect': 'The 5-Channel Sequencer runs email, phone, LinkedIn, SMS, and WhatsApp.'}
- {'category': 'Product plan names', 'rule': 'Title case for named pricing tiers: Free, Pay as You Go, MCP Unlimited, Team plan.', 'example_correct': 'The Team plan includes 10,000 execution credits.', 'example_incorrect': 'The team plan includes 10,000 execution credits.'}
- {'category': 'Framework and program names', 'rule': 'Title case for named frameworks and programs: Programmable Revenue Blueprint, Pipeline Architecture Standard, Sales Pipeline Maturity Model, Tenbound Standard.', 'example_correct': 'The Programmable Revenue Blueprint is $1,000.', 'example_incorrect': 'The programmable revenue blueprint is $1,000.'}
- {'category': 'Job roles and titles', 'rule': 'Lowercase when used generically in running text. Acronyms (SDR, AE, FDE, RevOps) always uppercase.', 'example_correct': 'An engineer sits with every role: SDR, AE, sales manager, growth, marketing.', 'example_incorrect': 'An Engineer sits with every role: SDR, AE, Sales Manager, Growth, Marketing.'}
- {'category': 'Section headers / numbered labels', 'rule': "Use '01 / Label' format for major section markers. The label is title case.", 'example_correct': '01 / The system', 'example_incorrect': '01 / THE SYSTEM'}
- {'category': 'Headlines and H1s', 'rule': 'Sentence case throughout — only the first word and proper nouns are capitalized.', 'example_correct': 'Your reps close deals. The CRM fills itself.', 'example_incorrect': 'Your Reps Close Deals. The CRM Fills Itself.'}


## Numbers Metrics

**Spell Out When:**
- Numbers at the start of a sentence when they describe a count of abstract items: 'Fifty three companies are on our client record'
- Ordinal references to weeks or steps in narrative prose: 'Week one we watch. Week two we write it down.'
- Time durations used conversationally in body copy: 'Thirty minutes with an account executive'

**Use Numerals When:**
- All prices and dollar figures: '$1,000,' '$99/mo,' '$5,000,' '$25,000'
- All credit, contact, and data volume counts: '1,000 contact reveals,' '10,000 execution credits,' '700M+ contacts,' '100M+ companies'
- Percentages and rates: '60% of target,' '0.35,' '4x ROI'
- Time frames used in specifications: '45 minutes each,' '5-day sprint,' '60 days,' '3 weeks'
- Role counts, session counts, and step counts in specs: 'up to 7 roles,' '25 sessions a month,' '4 campaigns'
- Version and plan labels: 'Level 1,' 'Level 2,' 'Step 01'
- Statistical or benchmark figures: '4.4 avg. rating,' '2,500+ clients,' '115+ case studies'

**Percentage Format:** Use the % symbol with no space: '60%', '99%'. In commission math, write the multiplier as a decimal: 'base salary x percent of target hit x 0.35'.
**Currency Format:** Dollar sign immediately before the numeral, no space: '$1,000', '$99', '$25,000'. Use '/mo' or '/user' as compact suffixes on pricing displays. Spell out 'per month' in running prose.
**Metrics Format:** Use the 'x' multiplier format: '4x ROI'. Use '+' suffix for approximate large numbers: '700M+', '2,500+', '30B+'. Use '10 years' not 'a decade' when the figure appears in a stat block, but 'a decade' is acceptable in narrative prose.
**Examples:**
- ✅ $99/mo, all included
- ✅ 700M+ verified B2B contacts
- ✅ 4x ROI, using the campaign calculator
- ✅ Fifty three companies are on our client record
- ✅ Three weeks. One engineer inside your team.
- ❌ 99 dollars per month, all included
- ❌ Seven hundred million plus verified B2B contacts
- ❌ 4 times ROI


## Punctuation

**Oxford Comma:** True
**Oxford Comma Example:** Email, phone, LinkedIn, SMS, and WhatsApp in automated sequences. / SDR, AE, sales manager, growth, and marketing.
**Em Dash Usage:** Em dashes are not used for parenthetical asides. Instead, the brand uses period breaks and fragment sentences to create rhythm. When a dash appears in UI display copy it is a mid-dot separator: 'Outbound . Active', 'Interested . No Meeting . Urgent'. Do not use em dashes as sentence interrupters in marketing copy.
**Exclamation Points:** Never used in marketing copy, product UI, or system messages. The brand does not use exclamation points. Confidence is conveyed through declarative statements, not punctuation energy.
**Quotation Marks:** Used for direct speech or example buyer dialogue in UI mockups: '"How does this compare to what we run today?"' Also used when introducing a term being defined: 'Ask two reps in the same segment to describe the ideal account.' Not used for scare quotes or to soften claims.
**Contractions:** Used freely and naturally throughout all copy. 'You're accountable for all six.' 'The ones you can't prove get argued about.' 'Nobody can say why.' 'We're' and 'you'll' are acceptable. Contractions make the voice feel like a practitioner talking, not a brochure.
**Additional Rules:**
- Semicolons are used in Tenbound body copy for closely related independent clauses: 'Every session is recorded and transcribed; that is how the analysis is done.'
- Colons are used to introduce lists and elaborations in feature callouts: 'Three ways in.' followed by a colon structure.
- Periods end fragment sentences used for emphasis: 'No seats. No contracts. Cancel anytime.'
- Slashes are used in plan/UI labels: '$99/mo', '$25/user', '01 / The system'. No spaces around slashes in compact labels; spaces used in section header format.
- Bullet points in feature lists do not end with periods when they are noun phrases. Full sentences within bullets do end with periods.


## Formatting

**Bold Usage:** Bold is used for key terms being introduced or defined within body copy, and for named labels in comparison tables (Use This / Not This). Not used for general emphasis in marketing paragraphs — the sentence structure itself carries emphasis.
**Italic Usage:** Italics appear on the Tenbound site for a single emphasized word within a headline to create visual contrast: 'The foundation you build on.' Used very sparingly. Not used for general emphasis.
**All Caps Policy:** All-caps is reserved exclusively for the brand name CIENCE and for acronyms (SDR, AE, FDE, CRM, ICP, GTM, MCP, CLI, CDP, ABM, SEO, AEO, QBR). Never used for emphasis in body copy or headlines.
**Underline Usage:** Underlines are reserved for hyperlinks only. Never used for emphasis in body copy.
**Bullet Points:** Used for feature lists, deliverable lists, and 'what you get' sections. Each bullet is a parallel noun phrase or short sentence. Bullets do not begin with a capital unless they are full sentences. Lists of three or fewer items are often written inline with commas instead.
**Numbered Lists:** Used for sequential steps, program stages, and ordered processes where sequence matters: 'Week 1 / Week 2 / Week 3', 'Step 01 / Step 02'. Labels use zero-padded two-digit numerals (01, 02, 03) in UI section markers. Prose step lists use spelled-out ordinals.
**Paragraph Length:** Body paragraphs run 2–4 sentences maximum. Single-sentence paragraphs and deliberate fragments are common and intentional for emphasis. Long explanatory passages (as on Tenbound) are broken into named sub-sections rather than extended paragraphs. The rule of thumb from the copy: if a sentence can stand alone, let it.

## Terminology

**Preferred Terms:**
- {'use_this': 'buyer graph', 'not_this': 'database / contact list / data platform', 'reason': "The term 'buyer graph' is the core product metaphor — a live, connected record, not a static list. Used consistently across graph8.com."}
- {'use_this': 'launch', 'not_this': 'campaign run / send / blast', 'reason': "graph8 uses 'launch' as the specific term for an initiated outbound motion, reflecting the system's end-to-end loop from signal to close."}
- {'use_this': 'execution credits', 'not_this': 'tokens / usage units / API calls', 'reason': "'Execution credits' is the pricing unit used across all plan descriptions. 'Contact credits' is the parallel term for data actions."}
- {'use_this': 'forward deployed engineer / FDE', 'not_this': 'consultant / analyst / advisor', 'reason': "Tenbound and CIENCE specifically distinguish their engineers from consultants and analysts: 'Not an analyst, not an account manager. The same person who would build it.'"}
- {'use_this': 'revenue ontology', 'not_this': 'data model / CRM schema / process documentation', 'reason': "The term 'revenue ontology' is a defined Tenbound concept covering objects, states, evidence, links, and permitted actions. It is explicitly differentiated from a CRM schema."}
- {'use_this': 'motion', 'not_this': 'process / workflow / cadence', 'reason': "'Motion' is the consistent term for an account's journey from first touch to handoff. 'The whole motion is written down and repeats in one system.'"}
- {'use_this': 'qualified meeting', 'not_this': 'booked meeting / demo / appointment', 'reason': "The distinction between a 'booked' and a 'qualified' meeting is central to Tenbound's framework. The two terms are not interchangeable."}
- {'use_this': 'signal', 'not_this': 'trigger / alert / data point', 'reason': "'Signal' is the consistent term for any buyer motion event — visitor, intent, hiring, job change, social, tech stack, funding. '2 billion signals daily.'"}
- {'use_this': 'in-market', 'not_this': 'active / interested / warm', 'reason': "'In-market' is used specifically to describe accounts showing buying signals: '42 in-market,' 'who is in-market.'"}
- {'use_this': 'seat fees / per-seat', 'not_this': 'per-user pricing / user licenses', 'reason': "The brand's differentiator is explicitly framed as 'no seat fees': 'Unlimited users, no seat fees.' 'Per-seat' is used when describing what competitors charge, not graph8."}
- {'use_this': 'data tax / seat tax / tool tax', 'not_this': 'costs / fees / overhead', 'reason': "These three compound terms are brand-specific framing for the problem graph8 solves: 'graph8 replaces the data tax, seat tax, and tool tax with one buyer graph.'"}
- {'use_this': 'held meeting', 'not_this': 'completed meeting / attended meeting', 'reason': "CIENCE pricing uses 'held-meeting fee' as the specific term for a meeting that took place, distinguishing it from a booked meeting."}

**Industry Jargon Policy:** GTM, SDR, AE, BDR, ICP, RevOps, MQL, SQL, ABM, CDP, CRM, MCP, CLI, FDE are used without definition in most contexts — the audience is assumed to be revenue professionals who know these terms. However, when introducing a less-common term (revenue ontology, buyer graph, FDE), define it in context on first use. Avoid jargon that sounds impressive but lacks operational meaning: 'leverage,' 'synergize,' 'holistic,' 'best-in-class.'
**Acronym Policy:** Spell out on first use when the term is specific to the brand's framework (FDE = forward deployed engineer, AEO = answer engine optimization). Standard B2B sales acronyms (SDR, AE, CRM, ICP, GTM) do not need to be spelled out. Acronyms are always uppercase. Do not create new acronyms for concepts that already have plain-language names.

## Product Naming

**Company Name:** graph8
**Company Name Never:**
- Graph8
- GRAPH8
- Graph 8
- graph 8

**Product Names:**
- graph8 Platform (the full product; often just 'graph8')
- CIENCE (managed GTM execution services brand — always all-caps)
- Tenbound (pipeline assessment and research brand — title case)
- My Desk (the rep's ranked daily work queue — title case, always two words)
- Team HQ (the leaderboard and activity feed — title case)
- Studio (the GTM content and strategy engine — capitalize as a standalone name)
- Buyer Graph (when used as a proper product noun; lowercase 'buyer graph' in generic descriptive use)
- Programmable Revenue Blueprint (Tenbound assessment product — full title case always)
- Pipeline Architecture Standard (Tenbound framework — full title case always)
- Sales Pipeline Maturity Model (Tenbound framework — full title case always)

**Feature Names:**
- Chief of Staff (AI agent — title case)
- SDR Agent (AI agent — title case)
- RevOps Agent (AI agent — title case)
- AE Cockpit (deal management surface — title case)
- MCP Server (developer integration — capitalize MCP, Server as a compound name)
- Sequencer (product surface — capitalize when named, lowercase when descriptive)
- Dialer (product surface — capitalize when named)
- AI Inbox (product surface — capitalize AI Inbox as a named feature)
- Waterfall enrichment (descriptive; 'Enrichment Waterfall' when used as a named feature label)
- GTM Setup Sprint (CIENCE service — title case)
- Performance-Driven Growth (CIENCE service — title case)


## Headlines

**H1 Rules:** Sentence case only. One declarative statement or a two-part punchy structure separated by a period. Lead with the customer's situation or outcome, not the product name. Often uses a fragment for the second beat: 'Your reps close deals. The CRM fills itself.' Max ~10 words per clause. The product or brand name is almost never in the H1.
**H2 Rules:** Sentence case. Used for major section introductions — often a benefit statement or a reframing of the problem. Frequently a single sentence or fragment: 'Every buyer signal becomes a launch.' 'One system senses buyer motion, launches the work, and closes revenue.' Can be longer and more explanatory than H1 when it introduces a complex concept.
**H3 Rules:** Sentence case. Used for named subsections within a major section. Often a noun phrase describing what follows: 'The four levels,' 'How it works,' 'What you get.' Can also be a direct question: 'Do you know what's capping your pipeline?' Kept short — typically 2–6 words.
**Headline Style:** Outcome-first and problem-aware. Headlines describe what the customer will experience or what problem is being solved — not what the feature is called. Fragments and short declarative sentences are preferred over complete grammatical sentences. No exclamation points. No superlatives without evidence. The best headlines on the sites read like a practitioner stating a fact.
**Examples:**
- ✅ Free data. Usage-based execution.
- ✅ Your revenue system, mapped. The foundation you build on.
- ✅ One system senses buyer motion, launches the work, and closes revenue.
- ✅ We build the revenue system, then we run it.
- ✅ Do you know what's capping your pipeline?
- ❌ Introducing graph8: The Revolutionary AI-Powered Sales Platform That Transforms Your Revenue!
- ❌ Leverage Our Cutting-Edge Solutions for Maximum Pipeline Growth


## Links Ctas

**Link Text Rules:** Link text describes the destination or action specifically. 'Read the Standard,' 'Read the sales pipeline maturity model,' 'See how the build works,' 'Back to CIENCE.' Never use 'click here,' 'learn more,' or 'read more' as standalone link text. Links in body copy are woven into the sentence naturally so the linked phrase describes what the reader will find.
**Button Text Rules:** Verb-first, outcome-specific, short. The most common primary CTA is 'Start Free' — two words, no punctuation. Secondary CTAs name the specific action: 'Book a meeting,' 'Buy now,' 'Join Demo,' 'Talk to an AE first.' Avoid generic verbs like 'Submit,' 'Go,' 'Learn More,' or 'Get Started' without a qualifier. Button text does not end with punctuation.
**Cta Examples:**
- {'context': 'Primary sign-up / platform entry', 'guidance': "Use 'Start Free' as the default. No exclamation, no 'trial' language unless specifying the 7-day trial. Keep to two words.", 'do_example': 'Start Free', 'dont_example': 'Sign Up Now!'}
- {'context': 'Demo or product walkthrough', 'guidance': "Name the format: 'Join Demo' for the live weekly demo. 'See My Desk in action' for a specific feature preview.", 'do_example': 'Join Demo', 'dont_example': 'Watch a Video'}
- {'context': 'Sales conversation / discovery', 'guidance': "Name the format and set expectations: 'Book a meeting' (CIENCE), 'Book a discovery call' (Tenbound), 'Talk to an AE first' (Tenbound). Never 'Contact Sales' or 'Request a Demo' without specificity.", 'do_example': 'Book a discovery call', 'dont_example': 'Contact Us'}
- {'context': 'Purchase / transactional', 'guidance': "Use 'Buy now' for direct purchase (Tenbound Blueprint at $1,000). Clear, transactional, no softening language.", 'do_example': 'Buy now', 'dont_example': 'Proceed to Checkout'}
- {'context': 'Secondary / exploratory', 'guidance': "Offer an alternative path in plain language: 'Talk to an AE first,' 'Or buy the blueprint,' 'Or score yourself first.' Use 'Or' to frame the secondary option as a genuine alternative, not a fallback.", 'do_example': 'Or score yourself first', 'dont_example': 'Not ready? Learn more here.'}


## System Messages

**Tone:** Calm, specific, and action-oriented. System messages reflect the same practitioner voice as marketing copy — no exclamation points, no filler, no apologetic hedging. State what happened and what is next.
**Length Guidance:** One sentence for toasts and confirmations. Two sentences maximum for states that require a next action. Empty states can include a short explanatory line plus a single CTA. Never use more words than the user needs to act.
**Examples:**
- {'type': 'Success / completion', 'guidance': 'State what completed and, if relevant, what happens next. Past tense for the action, present tense for the result.', 'example': 'Follow-ups sent. 9 emails delivered from maya@.'}
- {'type': 'Loading / in-progress', 'guidance': "Name the specific operation in progress, not generic 'Loading...' Reflect the system's own language: 'querying the graph,' 'enriching,' 'analyzing.'", 'example': 'Querying the buyer graph…'}
- {'type': 'Empty state', 'guidance': "Explain what this surface is for and offer the action to populate it. Mirror the product's plain-language style.", 'example': 'No signals yet. Connect your calendar and CRM to start seeing buyer motion here.'}
- {'type': 'Approval request', 'guidance': 'Name the action, state the risk level, describe what is not reversible. From the actual UI pattern: name the send count, the sender, the consequence.', 'example': 'Send 9 follow-ups from maya@. High risk — not reversible. Approve, edit, or reject.'}
- {'type': 'Agent action completed', 'guidance': 'Name the agent, name the action, give the count or outcome. Past tense.', 'example': 'SDR agent sent 9 follow-ups on #q4-outbound.'}


## Error Status

**Error Tone:** Factual and forward-looking. Do not apologize effusively. Name what stopped and why, then give the specific next action. The voice stays the same as the rest of the product — no exclamation points, no 'Oops!'
**Error Structure:** What stopped (one clause) + why or what is missing (one clause) + what to do next (one action). Modeled on the actual UI pattern: 'Blocked — RevOps agent: CRM owner missing on Atlas Bio.'
**Status Tone:** Present tense for ongoing operations, past tense for completed steps. Use the agent's name and the action verb. Consistent with the Activity feed style: 'SDR agent sent 9 follow-ups,' 'Chief of Staff updated 2 deal owners in the CRM.'
**Recovery Guidance:** Always provide a specific next action the user can take. Name the field, the step, or the person who can resolve the block. Never end on the error state alone. Model: 'Blocked — RevOps agent: CRM owner missing on Atlas Bio' implies the fix is to assign a CRM owner to that account.
**Examples:**
- {'type': 'Blocked agent action', 'guidance': 'Name the agent, name the specific missing condition, imply or state the fix.', 'example': 'Blocked — RevOps agent: CRM owner missing on Atlas Bio. Assign an owner to continue.'}
- {'type': 'Validation / missing input', 'guidance': "Name the missing field specifically. Do not use generic 'required field' language.", 'example': 'Work email is required to start free.'}
- {'type': 'Sync or integration error', 'guidance': 'Name the connected system and the specific failure. Offer one action.', 'example': 'HubSpot sync paused. Reconnect your HubSpot account to resume two-way updates.'}
- {'type': 'Rate limit / fair use', 'guidance': "Explain the limit's purpose honestly (as the pricing page does: 'They guard against scraping, not real GTM work'), then state the path to continue.", 'example': 'Credit limit reached for this action. Upgrade to the Team plan for 10,000 monthly execution credits — or wait for your cycle to reset.'}


## Ai Content Rules

**Disclosure Policy:** graph8 does not require explicit 'AI-generated' labels on standard product copy, UI text, or campaign content produced by AI agents within the platform. However, any AI-generated content presented as human-authored testimonials, case studies, or editorial commentary must be reviewed and approved by a human editor before publication.
**Review Requirements:** All AI-generated long-form content (blog posts, help docs, email sequences) requires human editorial review before publishing. Pricing copy, legal copy, and any content referencing specific credit counts or plan terms must always be human-verified for accuracy — AI should never autonomously publish these.
**Forbidden In Ai:**
- Fabricated customer quotes or testimonials
- Invented pricing figures or credit amounts
- Claims that a plan includes features it does not
- Overly promotional language that conflicts with graph8's direct tone (e.g., 'revolutionary', 'game-changing', 'world-class')
- Content that implies guaranteed outcomes from AI agents or campaigns

**Tone Consistency:** AI-generated content must match graph8's established voice: direct, fragment-friendly, no buzzwords, transparent about cost and limits. AI outputs that sound corporate, overly enthusiastic, or jargon-heavy must be edited to align with brand tone before use.
**Fact Checking:** All factual claims in AI-generated content — especially pricing figures, credit counts, plan names, and feature availability — must be verified against the current pricing page and product documentation before publication. AI must not invent or extrapolate pricing details.
**Personalization Rules:** AI personalization in outreach or campaigns should use verified contact data from graph8's own contact reveals. Personalization tokens (name, company, role) must be validated before send. Fallback defaults must always be defined to avoid broken or empty fields in delivered messages.

**Summary Rule:** Write like graph8 prices: plainly, transparently, and without waste. Lead with what's free, say what things cost, cut the rest — and never capitalize the 'g' in graph8.

# Brand Voice

## Portfolio scope: graph8, CIENCE, and Tenbound

Voice applies to graph8, CIENCE, and Tenbound. graph8 explains platform capabilities; CIENCE explains how execution is operated; Tenbound explains how pipeline problems are diagnosed. Tenbound's voice should be analytical, concrete, and educational: explain the framework, what the assessment examines, what the buyer receives, and what remains uncertain. Do not turn a Tenbound assessment into an implied graph8 software sales commitment.

---

# Brand Voice

**Voice Summary:** graph8 speaks with the authority of a decade of real B2B outbound data and the precision of an engineer who has watched how pipeline actually gets made — not how teams describe it. Across graph8 (the autonomous revenue platform), CIENCE (managed GTM execution), and Tenbound (pipeline assessment and research), the voice is direct, specific, and grounded in measurable outcomes. It names the problem plainly, states the fix without hedging, and earns trust by showing its work. There is no hype, no feature laundry lists, and no empty superlatives. When graph8 says "the CRM fills itself," it means every call, email, and meeting logs automatically on one buyer graph — and it can show you exactly how. The voice respects the intelligence of revenue leaders, RevOps practitioners, SDRs, and AEs who have been oversold and under-delivered before. It is confident without being arrogant, technical without being inaccessible, and ambitious without making promises it cannot keep. Whether describing an AI agent that clones a rep's voice, a forward-deployed engineer who shadows your sales team for three weeks, or a six-pillar framework for scoring your pipeline maturity, graph8 communicates with the same register: clear, honest, built on evidence, and always pointing toward execution.

## Voice In Three Words

- Direct
- Grounded
- Precise

## Tone Attributes

### Direct

**Attribute:** Direct
**Scale Position:** Blunt but not abrasive — confident without condescension
**Description:** graph8 says what it means in the fewest words that carry the full meaning. It does not soften claims with qualifiers or pad sentences with filler. When the system does something, it says so. When something is a problem, it names the problem. This directness applies across all three brands: graph8 platform feature pages, CIENCE managed service descriptions, and Tenbound assessment materials all lead with the plain statement before any explanation.

### Grounded

**Attribute:** Grounded
**Scale Position:** Evidence-led but not academic — always traceable to real outcomes
**Description:** Every claim connects to something observable: 700M+ verified contacts, ten years of CIENCE campaign data, 2 billion signals processed daily, a $1,000 three-week blueprint that produces five documents your team keeps. graph8 never makes a claim it cannot back with a number, a method, or a published standard. Tenbound's Pipeline Architecture Standard and Maturity Model are free to read precisely because grounding in evidence means being willing to show the work.

### Precise

**Attribute:** Precise
**Scale Position:** Technical enough to be credible — clear enough for a revenue leader with no engineering background
**Description:** graph8 uses exact language: 'Read, Propose, or Act mode,' 'waterfall enrichment,' 'revenue ontology,' 'execution credits.' These are not jargon deployed to impress — they are the accurate names for real system behaviors. When a term is introduced, its meaning is shown immediately through context or a brief definition, so precision never becomes a barrier. The same precision applies to pricing: $99/mo, $5,000 setup, $1,000 blueprint — no 'contact us for pricing' where a number can be stated plainly.

### Measured

**Attribute:** Measured
**Scale Position:** Calm confidence — never hype, never undersell
**Description:** graph8 does not use exclamation points to create excitement it has not earned. It does not call itself the '#1' anything or use superlatives without evidence. It lets the specificity of what the system does carry the weight. At the same time, it does not undersell: 'one buyer graph, signal to revenue' is a large claim made with calm conviction because the data and the ten-year track record behind CIENCE support it.

### Honest

**Attribute:** Honest
**Scale Position:** Forthright about limitations — honest framing builds more trust than polished spin
**Description:** graph8 tells buyers who the Programmable Revenue Blueprint is NOT for. Tenbound says plainly: 'Skip it if you want a number first.' The pricing page says 'fair-use rate limits apply.' CIENCE commission structures are spelled out in full, including when commission is not paid. This honesty is not a concession — it is the brand's sharpest differentiator in a market full of oversold platforms and underdelivered outcomes.

## Voice Characteristics

### Item 1

**Characteristic:** Problem-First Structure
**Definition:** Lead with the named problem before introducing the solution. The reader should recognize their own situation before graph8 explains what it does about it.
**Do Example:** Your data is scattered, stale, and rented. It lives in separate tools, goes stale the moment you export, and access is metered. Cleanup never ends.
**Dont Example:** Introducing graph8 Data — the revolutionary B2B contact intelligence solution that transforms how you prospect! Discover the power of our cutting-edge database today.

### Item 2

**Characteristic:** Concrete Over Abstract
**Definition:** Name the specific thing rather than the category. Use actual numbers, named features, and observable outcomes instead of abstract benefit language.
**Do Example:** Search 700M+ contacts and 100M+ companies by your ICP. Filter by title, seniority, industry, tech stack, and live intent. Free to search the whole network, no list to upload first.
**Dont Example:** Our comprehensive data platform gives you access to a vast universe of B2B contacts, enabling powerful prospecting capabilities across your entire total addressable market.

### Item 3

**Characteristic:** Short Sentence Rhythm
**Definition:** Use short, declarative sentences that build a logical sequence. Each sentence carries one complete idea. Long sentences are reserved for explanations that genuinely require multiple connected clauses.
**Do Example:** One buyer graph, free to search. 700M contacts and 100M companies, live and enriched, resolved to the person. Dedup and merge built in.
**Dont Example:** Our innovative buyer graph solution provides revenue teams with a comprehensive, unified, and always-current view of their total addressable market, including verified contact data, firmographic intelligence, technographic data, and real-time buyer intent signals, all accessible from one centralized platform.

### Item 4

**Characteristic:** Show the Work
**Definition:** Demonstrate how something works rather than asserting that it works. Use step sequences, numbered flows, and concrete examples to make the abstract tangible.
**Do Example:** The deal becomes a quote, the quote gets signed, billing provisions itself, the deal moves to won, and the commission lands. Agents run each step, your rep wins the close, and the whole flow stays on one buyer graph.
**Dont Example:** Our seamless end-to-end revenue workflow automation ensures frictionless deal progression from opportunity to closed revenue with minimal manual intervention.

### Item 5

**Characteristic:** Earned Authority
**Definition:** Reference real, verifiable evidence rather than generic credibility claims. Cite published frameworks, documented client counts, and verified ratings — never fabricated testimonials or inflated statistics.
**Do Example:** Fifty three companies are on our client record, Okta, LinkedIn, GitLab, Gong, Outreach and Salesloft among them, so we know which steps those teams handed to a workflow, which they left to people, and what broke when they got it wrong.
**Dont Example:** As a trusted leader in B2B revenue technology, our world-class platform has helped thousands of industry-leading enterprises achieve their growth goals through our proven methodology.

### Item 6

**Characteristic:** Buyer-Side Framing
**Definition:** Write from the buyer's perspective and current experience, not from the seller's perspective on what the product does. Name the buyer's symptoms before naming the solution category.
**Do Example:** Ask two reps in the same territory for their top twenty accounts. You get two different lists. Neither can be checked against anything. That is what a Manual pipeline costs you every week.
**Dont Example:** graph8's intelligent account prioritization module ensures consistent territory coverage and eliminates the inefficiencies associated with uncoordinated prospecting activities.

### Item 7

**Characteristic:** Explicit Trade Acknowledgment
**Definition:** Name what the buyer gives up to get the benefit. Honest trade framing signals that graph8 knows what it is asking and does not hide the cost of engagement.
**Do Example:** The trade: where your pipeline leaks and the fix for each, but your team implements it and gives 45 minutes per role.
**Dont Example:** With zero disruption to your existing workflow, our rapid onboarding process delivers instant value from day one, requiring virtually no time investment from your team.

## Writing Principles

### Item 1

**Principle:** Name the Problem Before the Product
**Explanation:** Revenue leaders have been pitched enough. They recognize their own problem faster than they recognize any vendor's solution. Leading with an accurate, specific description of a known pain — stale data, the CRM tax, manual account selection, two teams using 'qualified' to mean different things — earns the right to describe what graph8 does about it. This structure applies at every scale, from a homepage hero to a LinkedIn post to a Tenbound assessment framing page.
**Guidelines:**
- Open with the observable symptom, not the solution category: 'Pipeline in the CRM, quotes in a doc tool, billing re-keyed into Stripe by hand' before 'graph8 Revenue fixes this'
- Name the cost of the problem in concrete terms: 'The numbers you cannot get and the workflows you do not have are the same list'
- Use the buyer's own language for the problem, not vendor category terminology
- Apply this structure to CIENCE service pages (managed SDR limitations), Tenbound assessment pages (gaps nobody mapped), and graph8 platform pages equally


### Item 2

**Principle:** Pricing Is a Communication Tool, Not a Concession
**Explanation:** graph8 publishes pricing for every offering across all three brands. This is a deliberate voice decision: stating $99/mo, $5,000 GTM setup, $1,000 Programmable Revenue Blueprint, and full SDR level pricing by geography signals transparency and respect for the buyer's time. Hiding pricing behind 'contact us' implies there is something to hide. Showing pricing plainly — including commission structures and what happens below 60% of target — is an expression of the brand's honesty value.
**Guidelines:**
- State prices plainly without anchoring language or 'only' qualifiers
- Include what is and is not in the price in adjacent copy
- Name the exact dollar figure before the explanation of what it buys
- When a fee has conditions (commission tiers, per-SDR recruitment cost), state the conditions explicitly rather than summarizing them favorably


### Item 3

**Principle:** Specificity Is the Argument
**Explanation:** In a market full of platforms claiming to 'unify your revenue stack' and 'unlock AI-powered growth,' specificity is the only differentiator in language. The number 2 billion signals per day, the 44 documents Studio generates, the six pillars of the Pipeline Architecture Standard, the four maturity levels from Manual to Autonomous — these specifics are not marketing embellishments. They are the argument. Every claim should be traceable to a real system behavior, a published framework, or a documented dataset.
**Guidelines:**
- Use exact numbers whenever available: '700M+ contacts,' '500+ native integrations,' '10,000 execution credits,' '$9,500 Standard Build'
- Name the specific components of a process: 'SDR Agent, Chief of Staff, RevOps Agent' not 'AI agents'
- Describe features by what they do, not what they are: 'clones any rep voice for inbound and outbound calls with live booking' not 'AI voice capabilities'
- For Tenbound content, cite the Standard by name and note it is published and free to read
- Avoid round numbers that sound estimated when the real number is known


### Item 4

**Principle:** Humans and Agents Have Separate Roles — Name Both
**Explanation:** A persistent misconception in the AI-sales category is that automation replaces human judgment. graph8's voice explicitly rejects this framing because it is inaccurate to the product and unconvincing to the buyer. The brand describes exactly which steps agents run (research, drafting, enrichment, routing, logging) and exactly which steps stay human (the live conversation, the approval, the close). This is not a hedge — it is a genuine product design principle that should be reflected in every description of AI capabilities.
**Guidelines:**
- Describe AI agent actions by their specific function: 'drafts 9 follow-ups in your voice' not 'handles outreach automatically'
- Always name what the human retains: 'your rep wins the close' alongside 'the Deal Agent drafted the proposal'
- Use the Read / Propose / Act framing when describing agent modes — it is precise and self-explanatory
- For CIENCE content, name the five-agent layer (Research, Deliverability, Outbound, Lead Ops, Scheduling) alongside the human SDR who 'takes the conversation, qualifies, handles the objection, books the meeting'
- Never imply full automation of the sales process — the honest framing is also the more compelling one


### Item 5

**Principle:** Frameworks Earn Engagement; Products Earn Revenue
**Explanation:** Tenbound's Pipeline Architecture Standard and Sales Pipeline Maturity Model are free, published, and openly citeable. This is not a loss leader — it is a demonstration that the framework stands on its own before any purchase. graph8's voice treats educational content (the Programmable Revenue Community, the weekly research publication, the self-assessment tool) with the same rigor as product copy: specific, evidence-based, and structured to be immediately useful without a sales conversation. The brand earns trust through frameworks before it earns revenue through products.
**Guidelines:**
- When referencing the six pillars (Market, Signal, Message, Motion, Mastery, Measurement), describe each by what it hands to the next — they are a chain, not a list
- Note that the Standard is free to read and cite with attribution; this transparency is part of the brand's credibility
- The four maturity levels (Manual, Assisted, Orchestrated, Autonomous) should be used consistently as a shared vocabulary across all three brands
- Community and research content should be framed as genuine contributions, not as lead-generation vehicles


### Item 6

**Principle:** Do Not Invent What You Cannot Prove
**Explanation:** graph8 does not fabricate performance statistics, claim certifications it does not hold, or attribute results to named clients without documented evidence. When evidence exists (CIENCE's review platform ratings, client logos, the 2,500+ brands served figure), it is cited precisely. When a number would require estimation, the brand uses the actual known figure or states the limitation clearly. This principle protects credibility and is a natural extension of the honesty tone attribute.
**Guidelines:**
- Use only documented proof points: '4.4 avg rating across 8 review platforms,' '115+ case studies,' '2,500+ clients served,' '250+ industries'
- When quoting from Tenbound's practitioner interview archive, attribute the source and methodology (e.g., Ryan Reisert, Buckets methodology, Tenbound interview archive)
- Do not imply results that the system cannot guarantee — 'signals that start the work' is accurate; 'signals that guarantee meetings' is not
- For new or emerging product features, describe what the system does, not what it will eventually achieve


## Word Choice

**Preferred Words:**
- one graph
- buyer graph
- execution
- signal
- launch
- motion
- pipeline
- revenue ontology
- forward deployed
- grounded
- verified
- resolved
- enriched
- live
- auto-launch
- qualify
- handoff
- plain
- direct
- measurable
- owned
- auditable
- logged
- one record
- one system
- one flow
- pay for execution
- no seat fees
- cancel anytime
- free to search
- yours to implement
- no vendor on the other side

**Avoided Words:**
- revolutionary
- game-changing
- disruptive
- world-class
- best-in-class
- synergy
- leverage (as a verb)
- holistic
- robust
- scalable solution
- empower
- unlock
- seamless
- frictionless
- cutting-edge
- innovative
- transformative
- next-generation
- AI-powered (without specifying what the AI does)
- streamline
- end-to-end solution
- comprehensive platform
- one-stop shop
- trusted partner
- industry-leading
- proven methodology (without citing the proof)

**Jargon Policy:** Use precise technical terms when they are the accurate name for a real system behavior or framework concept, and always make the meaning available through immediate context. Terms like 'revenue ontology,' 'buyer graph,' 'waterfall enrichment,' 'execution credits,' 'ICP,' 'AEO,' and 'MCP server' are used because they are exact — not because they signal sophistication. Introduce each term with a brief functional definition on first use within any document. Avoid borrowed enterprise-software jargon ('synergize,' 'leverage,' 'holistic,' 'robust,' 'scalable solutions') that adds no meaning. Do not use category buzzwords ('revolutionary,' 'game-changing,' 'best-in-class') as substitutes for specific claims.
**Acronym Policy:** Spell out acronyms on first use within a document, then use the abbreviation freely: Sales Development Representative (SDR), Ideal Customer Profile (ICP), Go-to-Market (GTM), Account Executive (AE), Revenue Operations (RevOps), Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE), Answer Engine Optimization (AEO), Model Context Protocol (MCP). Acronyms that are the product's own named constructs — like FDE, MCP — should be defined early because they are graph8-specific. Standard industry acronyms (CRM, B2B, API, CLI, CDP) may be used without definition in contexts where the audience clearly knows them.

## Grammar Preferences

- Use active voice for all agent and system actions: 'Studio generates 44 documents' not '44 documents are generated by Studio'
- Use second person (you / your) when addressing the buyer and first person plural (we / our) when speaking as graph8, CIENCE, or Tenbound — do not mix perspectives within a section
- Do not use the Oxford comma inconsistently — the brand uses it: 'email, phone, LinkedIn, SMS, and WhatsApp'
- Use numerals for all numbers, including those below ten, when they appear alongside data, pricing, or measurements: '2 billion signals,' '5-day sprint,' '3 weeks,' '7 roles'
- Write out 'million' and 'billion' rather than abbreviating to M and B in running prose; abbreviate only in data callouts and UI labels: '700M+' in a data callout, '700 million' in a sentence
- Use the present tense for system behaviors: 'Studio learns your business, builds the strategy, generates every deliverable' — not 'will learn,' 'will build,' 'will generate'
- Avoid nominalization: 'graph8 executes the campaign' not 'graph8 enables campaign execution'
- Spell out 'and' rather than using '&' in running text; '&' is acceptable only in UI labels, navigation items, and data callouts
- Use 'that' for restrictive clauses (no comma) and 'which' for non-restrictive clauses (with comma); do not use 'which' where 'that' is correct
- Do not use 'leverage' as a verb; use 'use,' 'apply,' 'run on,' or 'draw from' instead

## Formatting Guidelines

- Use numbered section prefixes (01 /, 02 /, 03 /) for multi-part product and service pages to give readers a clear map before they scroll
- Use the em dash ( — ) sparingly to set off a clause that expands or clarifies the preceding statement — not as a stylistic tic
- Use sentence case for headlines and subheadings: 'Pay for execution, not seats' not 'Pay For Execution, Not Seats'
- Use the period inside the sentence, not as a dramatic fragment device — avoid stylistic one-word sentences used purely for rhythm
- Use bullet lists for feature inventories and step-by-step processes; use prose for argument and explanation
- Bold only terms being defined or contrasted, not for general emphasis — 'instrumented · A system carries it / manual · A person carries it / broken · Nothing carries it'
- Use slash notation for process flows: 'Sense the signal / Launch the motion / Run the conversation / Build pipeline / Close / Learn'
- Pricing is always stated as a number first: '$99 / mo' not 'just $99 per month' or 'starting at $99'
- Do not use exclamation points in product or service copy; enthusiasm is carried by specificity, not punctuation
- Use 'graph8' in all lowercase in running text, regardless of sentence position — the brand name is always lowercase
- When referencing the three brands together, list them as: graph8, CIENCE, and Tenbound — in that order, preserving each brand's own capitalization convention

**Audience Adaptations:** graph8, CIENCE, and Tenbound serve four primary audiences, each requiring a calibrated version of the core voice:

**Revenue Leaders (VPs of Sales, CROs, Founders):** Receive the highest density of outcome language and framework references. They care about the number, who owns the gaps, and what the next level of maturity costs them. Tenbound content (Pipeline Architecture Standard, Maturity Model, Programmable Revenue Blueprint) is written primarily for this audience. Use the six-pillar framework (Market, Signal, Message, Motion, Mastery, Measurement) as shared vocabulary. Lead with the yearly cost of a broken pillar before describing the fix.

**Revenue Operations and Sales Enablement:** Receive the most technical specificity about system behavior: revenue ontology definitions, CRM sync architecture, agent modes (Read / Propose / Act), waterfall enrichment logic, and integration details. This audience reads the setup document and the integration gaps deliverable. Use precise field-level language and name the systems that connect (Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive, Outreach, Salesloft, Stripe). Do not simplify technical details for this audience — they will catch inaccuracies.

**Sales Development Representatives and Account Executives:** Receive practical, daily-workflow framing. My Desk, Team HQ, the AI Inbox, the Dialer, and the SDR Agent are described in terms of what they see when they open the app on a Tuesday morning — a ranked queue, a drafted reply, a briefed meeting card. Avoid framework-heavy language; emphasize what the system does so the rep can spend their time on the live conversation.

**Builders and Developers:** Receive the most API-forward framing. The MCP Server, CLI, and open API are described in terms of what can be scripted, queried, or extended. Code-adjacent language (query, reveal, export, script, endpoint) is appropriate. The developer audience does not need the problem-first emotional structure as heavily — they respond to capability specificity and open-stack flexibility.

Across all audiences, the three brand voices remain consistent in their honesty, precision, and outcome orientation — only the ratio of framework language to operational language shifts.

# Brand Brief

## Portfolio scope: graph8, CIENCE, and Tenbound

The graph8 organization has three distinct brands: graph8 provides software and buyer-data infrastructure; CIENCE provides managed GTM execution; Tenbound provides pipeline assessment and research. Tenbound's role is to help revenue leaders understand their pipeline architecture and decide what to improve, using the Pipeline Architecture Standard, Sales Pipeline Maturity Model, and Programmable Revenue Blueprint. This brand brief covers that diagnostic role as well as the platform and services businesses.

---

# Brand Brief

**Company Name:** graph8

**Industry:** B2B SaaS

**Founded:** 2024

**Headquarters:** 360 NW 27th St, Miami, FL 33127, USA

**Mission:** graph8 exists to replace the fragmented, seat-taxed, tool-sprawling GTM stack with a single autonomous revenue system — one buyer graph that connects signals, data, campaigns, AI agents, pipeline, and human judgment so B2B teams can build and close revenue without the operational drag of managing eight disconnected tools.

**Vision:** By 2030, graph8 becomes the default operating system for B2B revenue teams — the single platform where every signal resolves to a real person, every launch runs autonomously from first intent to closed deal, and every organization can move from Manual to Autonomous maturity on the Tenbound Pipeline Architecture Standard. graph8, CIENCE, and Tenbound together serve tens of thousands of B2B companies across the full spectrum of need: self-serve platform users, fully managed GTM execution clients, and revenue leaders who demand a rigorous engineering-led assessment before committing to scale.

## Brand Essence

**Tagline:** One graph. Signal to revenue.
**Brand Promise:** graph8 promises that every buyer signal — from an anonymous site visit to a job-change alert to a social post — resolves to a real person, triggers the right motion automatically, and flows to closed revenue on a single buyer graph, with no data tax, no seat tax, and no tool sprawl.
**Unique Value:** graph8 is the only platform that unifies B2B data intelligence, omnichannel campaign execution, AI voice and inbox automation, native CRM with quote-to-cash, team collaboration with embedded AI agents, GTM content generation via Studio, and managed SDR services under one buyer graph — complemented by Tenbound's Pipeline Architecture Standard and Programmable Revenue Blueprint for teams that need to diagnose before they build.

## Core Values

### Item 1

**Value:** One Graph, One Truth
**Meaning:** Every product, agent, and human operator in the graph8 system reads from and writes to a single buyer graph. Fragmentation is not tolerated — not in data, not in workflow, not in reporting. The single record is the non-negotiable design constraint.
**Behaviors:**
- Every platform module (Data, Signals, Campaigns, Dialer, AI Inbox, CRM, Studio, Work) shares the same underlying buyer graph record
- Signals from visitors, intent, hiring, job changes, social, and engagement all flow into one scored stream
- The CRM fills itself from real activity — no manual re-keying, no nightly sync jobs
- Two-way sync with Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive, Outreach, and Salesloft preserves compatibility without forking the truth


### Item 2

**Value:** Execution Over Observation
**Meaning:** graph8 does not sell reports or dashboards that end at insight. Every signal, every piece of data, every strategy document produced by Studio is designed to trigger action — a launch, a sequence, a call, a booked meeting. The system is measured by revenue closed, not by data surfaced.
**Behaviors:**
- Usage-based pricing means customers pay only when the system executes — credits are spent on sends, calls, and agent runs, not on browsing data
- Signals auto-launch campaigns when a match is found; My Desk ranks the day's actions by urgency and deal value
- CIENCE's managed services are measured against held meetings and pipeline outcomes, not activity reports
- Tenbound's Programmable Revenue Blueprint delivers five implementable documents, not a presentation deck


### Item 3

**Value:** Human Judgment at the Right Moment
**Meaning:** Automation without control is a liability. graph8 is designed so AI agents run the volume — research, drafting, enrichment, routing, logging — while humans take the live conversation, the approval, and the close. Every AI action is logged, auditable, and reversible.
**Behaviors:**
- AI agents operate in Read, Propose, or Act modes with configurable guardrails set by the org
- High-risk actions (sending emails, spending credits, deleting records) always require approval unless explicitly enabled
- CIENCE's hybrid SDR model puts five AI agents beside one human SDR, so the human takes the conversation that needs judgment
- Tenbound's FDE program watches real workflows on a real screen — not a process document — because the real work is what gets written down


### Item 4

**Value:** Grounded in Real Revenue Data
**Meaning:** graph8's AI was not trained on the internet. It was trained on a decade of CIENCE campaign performance across millions of real B2B conversations, calls, and closed deals. Every scoring model, every agent, every playbook template is shaped by what actually converted — not by synthetic benchmarks.
**Behaviors:**
- 700M+ verified contacts and 100M+ companies enriched from real campaign feedback loops
- 30 billion intent signals processed monthly, scored against real conversion outcomes
- Tenbound's Pipeline Architecture Standard was developed from CIENCE client engagements across 2,500+ B2B brands
- Studio generates campaign strategies and content performance estimates grounded in historical campaign data


### Item 5

**Value:** Radical Pricing Transparency
**Meaning:** The B2B software industry runs on seat taxes, data taxes, and hidden upsells. graph8 refuses that model. Data is free to search. Pricing scales with execution, not with headcount. Contracts are month-to-month. Every fee — platform, SDR commission structure, per-meeting charges — is published and explained.
**Behaviors:**
- 700M+ contacts free to search on every plan; credits are spent only when data is revealed or execution runs
- Team plan at $99/mo includes unlimited users — pricing never scales with headcount
- CIENCE publishes SDR commission logic, per-meeting fee calculation, and onboarding costs on the pricing page
- Tenbound's Programmable Revenue Blueprint is a flat $1,000 with no vendor commitment on the other side


## Personality Traits

### Item 1

**Trait:** Direct and Precise
**Description:** graph8 communicates the way an engineer explains a system: with specificity, without filler. Claims are grounded in numbers (700M+ contacts, 2B signals daily, $99/mo for unlimited users). Vague category language is avoided. If something costs money, the cost is stated. If a limitation exists, it is named.
**Examples:**
- Pricing pages publish exact credit rates, SDR commission tiers, and fee calculation formulas
- Product pages show working UI mockups with real field names, not stock photography
- Tenbound's Blueprint page lists the exact five deliverables a buyer receives, verbatim


### Item 2

**Trait:** Confident Without Arrogance
**Description:** graph8 has strong conviction about how revenue systems should be built — one graph, autonomous execution, human judgment at the right moment — and states that conviction plainly. But it does not mock competitors or overstate outcomes. The attitude is that of a senior engineer who has seen what works and is willing to show the work.
**Examples:**
- Competitive positioning names what graph8 replaces (Salesforce for pipeline, PandaDoc for quotes, Gong for conversation intelligence) without disparaging those brands
- Tenbound's scoring methodology is published in full and free to read, so any score can be argued with
- CIENCE's proof section shows ratings across eight review platforms without cherry-picking only the highest scores


### Item 3

**Trait:** Technically Fluent
**Description:** graph8 speaks the language of revenue operations, developer tooling, and AI infrastructure simultaneously. It is comfortable with MCP servers, revenue ontologies, waterfall enrichment, and deal stage probabilities in the same conversation — because its buyers span RevOps leaders, sales engineers, and platform builders.
**Examples:**
- The platform exposes an MCP Server for Claude, Cursor, and ChatGPT; a CLI for terminal scripting; and a full REST API
- Tenbound's revenue ontology framework defines objects, states, evidence requirements, links, and permitted agent actions with engineering precision
- Studio generates design tokens exported as tokens.json alongside brand briefs and email sequences


### Item 4

**Trait:** Earnestly Useful
**Description:** graph8 would rather give a buyer the tool to diagnose their own problem than oversell a solution they are not ready for. The Tenbound Pipeline Architecture Standard is free to read. The self-assessment is free to take. The CIENCE Discovery Call has no pitch deck. The philosophy is: if the answer is honest, the right customer will buy.
**Examples:**
- Tenbound's Blueprint page explicitly says 'there is nothing to buy from us on the other side of the plan'
- The Pipeline Maturity Model section tells readers when NOT to buy the Blueprint
- graph8's free tier gives 1,000 contact reveals and 500 execution actions before asking for a credit card


## Primary Audience

**Segment:** B2B Revenue & Go-To-Market Teams
**Description:** Sales leaders, revenue operations professionals, and marketing teams at B2B companies — ranging from high-growth startups to enterprise organizations — who are responsible for building and scaling predictable outbound and inbound pipeline. These are data-savvy practitioners who are frustrated by fragmented sales tech stacks, poor data quality, and inefficient manual outreach processes. They are actively seeking a unified platform that combines reliable contact intelligence, real-time buyer intent signals, and automated multi-channel campaign execution to hit aggressive growth targets.
**Needs:**
- High-quality, verified B2B contact and company data at scale
- Real-time buyer intent and signal detection to prioritize outreach
- Multi-channel campaign automation across email, phone, LinkedIn, SMS, and WhatsApp
- AI-powered tools to increase rep productivity and reduce manual tasks
- Consolidated sales tech stack to reduce costs and complexity
- Accurate enrichment and data hygiene for their CRM and pipelines
- Actionable insights to identify in-market buyers before competitors do


## Secondary Audiences

### Revenue Builders and Platform Developers

**Segment:** Revenue Builders and Platform Developers
**Description:** Software engineers, RevOps architects, and technical founders who want to build revenue workflows or products on top of the graph8 infrastructure rather than use its pre-built applications.
**Needs:**
- MCP Server access to query the buyer graph from Claude, Cursor, and ChatGPT
- CLI for scripting search, reveal, and export operations in automated pipelines
- REST API and 500+ connector integrations for custom workflow orchestration
- Data warehouse connectivity and CDP capabilities for bringing their own enrichment vendors


### SMB and Growth-Stage B2B Teams

**Segment:** SMB and Growth-Stage B2B Teams
**Description:** Founders, heads of growth, and early sales leaders at companies with fewer than 100 employees who are building their outbound motion for the first time and need a complete GTM system without the cost of a fragmented enterprise stack.
**Needs:**
- A free entry point to explore 700M+ contacts without a credit card
- A full-platform solution at $99/mo with unlimited users and no seat fees
- CIENCE's GTM Setup Sprint ($5,000 one-time) to get four campaigns live in five days
- Tenbound's Programmable Revenue Blueprint ($1,000) to map the revenue system before scaling


**Market Position:** graph8 occupies the emerging category of Autonomous Revenue Systems — above point-solution competitors in data (ZoomInfo, Apollo.io, Cognism), engagement (Outreach, Salesloft, Reply.io), intent (6sense, Bombora), CRM (Salesforce, HubSpot), and AI SDR agents (11x.ai, Artisan AI) by unifying all of these capabilities on a single buyer graph with usage-based execution pricing. Unlike consolidation platforms that bundle existing products, graph8 is architected from a single data layer outward — meaning every signal, contact, conversation, deal, quote, and agent action writes to the same record. CIENCE adds a managed-services layer that no pure-software competitor can match at equivalent depth, and Tenbound adds a research and assessment layer that gives the combined offering credibility and methodology that AI-native competitors lack entirely.

## Key Differentiators

- Single buyer graph architecture: every module — Data, Signals, Campaigns, Dialer, AI Voice, AI Inbox, CRM, Quotes, Studio, Work, Analytics — reads and writes the same record, eliminating sync lag, integration debt, and conflicting sources of truth
- Usage-based execution pricing with no per-seat fees: the Team plan at $99/mo includes unlimited users, all features, and 10,000 execution credits — pricing scales with what graph8 does, not with how many people use it
- AI agents with configurable human control: Chief of Staff, SDR Agent, and RevOps Agent run in Read, Propose, or Act mode with org-set guardrails — every action is logged, auditable, and the approval step is built into the workflow, not bolted on
- Decade of real campaign training data: graph8's AI is shaped by ten years of CIENCE outbound across 2,500+ B2B brands and millions of live conversations — not a generic large language model applied to sales
- Managed execution via CIENCE: GTM Setup Sprint, Performance-Driven Growth, SDR Capacity (three levels, three geographies), Inbound Optimization, Scaled Outbound, and Audience Data give customers a fully staffed GTM team when software alone is not enough
- Engineering-led revenue assessment via Tenbound: the Programmable Revenue Blueprint ($1,000, three weeks) sends a forward-deployed engineer to shadow every sales role and deliver five implementable documents — ontology, gaps, maturity readout, setup spec, and improvement proposal — with no vendor commitment on the other side
- Published open frameworks: the Tenbound Pipeline Architecture Standard (six pillars) and Sales Pipeline Maturity Model (four levels) are free to read and use, giving graph8 intellectual authority in revenue system design that no pure-software competitor has established
- Full developer surface: MCP Server, CLI, REST API, and 500+ integrations allow technical buyers to query the buyer graph from any AI tool or build their own products on the graph8 infrastructure

**Origin Story:** graph8 was built on the back of a decade of real B2B outbound at CIENCE — millions of calls, emails, and meetings run for 2,500+ brands across enterprise, software, finance, and services. That campaign archive became the training data, the playbook library, and the proof base that no generic AI model could replicate. Tenbound contributed the intellectual framework: the Pipeline Architecture Standard and the Sales Pipeline Maturity Model, born from observing exactly where revenue systems break across six pillars. The result is a company that does not just sell software — it sells a system, built from evidence, run end to end.

**Brand Narrative:** The B2B revenue stack is broken by design. A team buys intent data from one vendor, exports a CSV, uploads it to a sequencer from a second vendor, routes the reply to a CRM from a third, generates a quote in a doc tool, re-keys the signature into a billing system by hand, and tries to forecast from a spreadsheet that is already stale by Monday. Every tool is right on its own terms. The stack as a whole is a liability — in integration debt, in seat fees, in manual handoffs, and in the definitions that live in people's heads instead of the systems that are supposed to run on them.

graph8 was built to end that. Not by acquiring a set of point solutions and bundling them under one logo, but by building a single buyer graph outward — one live record per buyer that every signal, every agent, every campaign, every deal, every quote, and every outcome writes to and reads from. When a visitor hits a pricing page three times, the buyer graph resolves them to a real person, scores the intent, and surfaces the signal in My Desk before a rep has to ask. When a deal closes, the quote fires, the e-signature triggers billing, and the commission logs — without a person re-keying anything between steps.
